# ARX VOICE SCRIPT — every spoken line in the Dawnlands

*Generated by `npx tsx tools/voice/sheet.mts` — edit the dialogue defs,
actor defs, `tools/voice/quips.json` or `tools/voice/characters.json`,
never this file.*

**139 characters · 1045 dialogue lines · 417 ambient barks · 144 quips.**

## How to record

- One file per line. Name it EXACTLY the backticked slug, e.g. `fen_bench__hub.wav`.
- Drop finished takes in `voicework/recorded/<character_id>/` in the game repo.
  WAV or OGG, mono, 48 kHz or 44.1 kHz, quiet room, no music bed. A human take
  always beats a generated one: the importer prefers `recorded/` over `generated/`.
- Read the character direction first, then the line. The blockquote is the exact
  transcript: say every word, no more, no fewer. `...` is a held pause, not a skip.
- Barks must be VERBATIM — the game matches the audio to the displayed line by its text.
- Quips are color, not scripts: a grunt slot like `bark` can be half a breath.
- To give a character a cloned voice of your own: record 10 to 20 seconds of clean
  speech, drop it at `~/code/voicelab/voices/<anything>.wav`, and set that name as
  `ttsVoice` in `tools/voice/characters.json`.

## The pipeline

```
npx tsx tools/voice/sheet.mts                  regenerate this sheet
npx tsx tools/voice/generate.mts [actor...]    Chatterbox lane -> voicework/generated/
npx tsx tools/voice/import.mts [actor...]      both lanes -> the live voice ledger
```

ford town's daily faces. Quips are authored for all twelve.

## Elder Rowan `elder_rowan` — 15 dialogue lines, 15 quips and barks

*Has greeted every waker for forty years. Remembers most of their names.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeper of the Waking Ring, the first voice every new arrival hears. Grandfatherly and unhurried; he has welcomed hundreds of wakers and carries the ones who didn't come back. Full warm sentences, old-fashioned turns, calls you 'child' or 'waker'. Practical wisdom, never cosmic. Warm, low, steady pace.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/king_bob` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

- `elder_rowan__bark_3` — "Forty years of wakers, and not one of them stayed. That's as it should be."

### Conversation: `q_the_lay_of_the_land_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_lay_of_the_land:available)*

**`q_the_lay_of_the_land_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've your feet under you now, child. I can see it from the porch. Time you saw the ford-town. Amberford, east down the lane, where the river slows enough to argue with. Will you go?

**`q_the_lay_of_the_land_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll go. What's there?"*

> A gate, a market, and more people than you've met all together. Find the North Gate and the captain who keeps it, Aldis. Tell her a waker walked the whole way. She'll know what that's worth.

**`q_the_lay_of_the_land_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not yet."*

> Then sit a while longer, child. The road east keeps.

### Conversation: `rowan_awakening`

**`rowan_awakening__wake`** — *opens the conversation*

> There you are. Breathe slow. The Ring's cold lets go quicker if you don't fight it. Up now. Let's have a look at you.

**`rowan_awakening__stones`** — *follows straight on from "wake"*

> I'm Rowan. I keep this village, and I keep the Ring: the five stones behind you. Folk step out of them the way you just did, a few every season, going back longer than anyone's grandmother. Where you were before this morning is gone. It's gone for all of you. We stopped asking the stones long ago. They've never once answered.

**`rowan_awakening__hub`** — *follows straight on from "stones"; or follows straight on from "village"; or follows straight on from "memory"*

> Ask your questions, child. Everyone has the same three, and I never tire of them.

**`rowan_awakening__village`** — *player says: "Where am I?"*

> Dawnmead. A green, a brook, and more chickens than people. We're the last soft ground before the frontier. East of our hedgerows the land runs wild for miles. Wakers rest here, learn their hands, then take the road. You will too. They all do.

**`rowan_awakening__memory`** — *player says: "Why can't I remember anything?"*

> None of you can. You came through with a pack on your back, strength in your limbs, and your own name, and nothing else. Some say the stones take memory as their toll. Old Hobb says you're likely better off without whatever it was. For my part, I mind what you do next, child. That part is yours entire.

**`rowan_awakening__guidance`** — *player says: "What should I do now?"*

> Three people, then the road. Bryn drills in the south yard. She'll wake up those arms. Iona keeps the fire by the cottages. She'll teach you to feed yourself. And look in your pack before you see either: axe, pick, blade, bow, and a staff. Heavier than you thought, isn't it? Go learn them. Then come back to me.

**`rowan_awakening__gift`** — *follows straight on from "guidance"*

> And take this: bread. Baked fresh this morning. Welcome to the world, waker. Most of it is kinder than it looks.

### Conversation: `rowan_green`

**`rowan_green__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "ring"; or follows straight on from "pointers"*

> There you are, waker. How's the day treating you?

**`rowan_green__ring`** — *player says: "Tell me about the Waking Ring."*

> Five stones, older than any map of them. They sleep for a week, sometimes a season. Then one dawn the frost melts off them in a ring, and someone new is standing where you stood. There are ruined gates in the deep wild that look like kin to our stones. I saw one once, years back. I didn't linger.

**`rowan_green__pointers`** — *player says: "Who should I see before I go?"*

> Bryn's in the south yard if your arms want work. Iona's at her fire. Fen will talk your ear off about his bench, bless him, and Hobb will find you something useful if you stand at his gate long enough. Small village. One good day covers it.

**`rowan_green__road`** — *player says: "I'm ready for the road east."*

> Then you're ready, and I won't keep you. The lane east crosses the brook and becomes the First Road. Follow it and you'll raise Amberford, the ford town, inside a day's walk. Rest at the wayfarers' lanterns when the light goes. And take this: coins. Bread money for the road. The Ring chose well this time. Go on, child.

**`rowan_green__road_again`** — *player says: "About the road east."*

> East over the brook, and keep near the lamps after dark. Eat before you set out, too. The road is poor company on an empty stomach.

## Farmer Hobb `farmer_hobb` — 9 dialogue lines, 15 quips and barks

*Talks to the cows. Swears they answer, and honestly, they might.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** The most gloriously boring man alive, and content. Wants rain at the right time. Short flat statements about immediate things: weather, hens, fence posts. Deliver absolutely deadpan; any wisdom is an accident and he'd deny it.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/court_phil` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.622 · cfg 0.586

### Conversation: `hobb_farm`

**`hobb_farm__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "produce"; or follows straight on from "practice"*

> Mind the latch. Bess leans on it when she's bored. Something you need?

**`hobb_farm__produce`** — *player says: "What do the animals give?"*

> Cow gives milk if you walk up gentle. Bess allows it, mostly. Hens drop eggs. Check the coop floor, mornings are best. Berries by the brook. That's breakfast, and nothing had to bleed for it.

**`hobb_farm__practice`** — *player says: "Mind if I practice my swings out here?"*

> Not on my animals. The old shed past the ford has rats in it. Bryn will tell you the same. If a hen squares up to you anyway, pay her no mind. She does that.

**`hobb_farm__pip`** — *player says: "Who's the small loud one?"*

> That's Pip. Mine. He has questions for everyone who comes off the stones, and you'll hear them whether you answer or not. He means nothing by it.

**`hobb_farm__farewell`** — *player says: "Just admiring the farm."*

> Aye. It's a good little patch. Latch! Sorry. Habit.

### Conversation: `q_hobbs_hens_offer` *(plays when: quest:hobbs_hens:available)*

**`q_hobbs_hens_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Market day's coming and I'm eight eggs short. The hens know it, too. They lay where they please. Coop, mostly. Long grass by the pasture, some days. Fetch me eight?

**`q_hobbs_hens_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll find your eggs."*

> Good. Mind the latch.

**`q_hobbs_hens_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I've bigger things to do."*

> Than eggs. All right.

### Conversation: `q_hobbs_hens_turnin` *(plays when: quest:hobbs_hens:ready)*

**`q_hobbs_hens_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Eight. All sound. That's market day saved, and Bess none the wiser why I'm pleased. Here.

## Iona `hearthkeeper_iona` — 16 dialogue lines, 15 quips and barks

*Smells of woodsmoke and berry preserve. The fire listens to her.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Hearthkeeper; feeds everyone and lost someone to the road she never names. Plain, kind, food-first. Homely comparisons only: bread, weather, the pot. No cleverness at all; warmth is the whole instrument.

**Chatterbox casting:** `news/matron_michele` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.551

### Conversation: `iona_fireside`

**`iona_fireside__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "fires"; or follows straight on from "where"*

> Pot's warm, love. What do you need?

**`iona_fireside__fires`** — *player says: "What else can a fire do?"*

> Anything you catch, a fire makes better: chicken, beef, the brook's fish once you've the patience for a rod. Any village fire will serve a traveller, and out in the wild you'll learn to build your own. It's the same knack everywhere.

**`iona_fireside__where`** — *player says: "Where do the berries grow?"*

> South of the bridge, along the near bank: berries, fibre, sageroot. Take a full pocket. The bank never minds.

**`iona_fireside__spare`** — *player says: "Anything warm to spare?"*

> Go on then, once. cooked chicken Careful, it's hot. After this you cook your own. I'm not being hard on you, love. I just want you able to manage.

**`iona_fireside__farewell`** — *player says: "Just warming my hands."*

> Warm hands, dry boots. Go on now.

### Conversation: `iona_hearth`

**`iona_hearth__warm`** — *opens the conversation*

> Come to the fire, love. The Ring leaves a chill in new folk. Takes half a day to shake. I'm Iona. I keep this hearth, and I'll teach you the first thing worth knowing out here: how to feed yourself.

**`iona_hearth__forage`** — *follows straight on from "warm"*

> Easiest meal there is: the berry bushes along the brook, just east of here. Walk up and pick. They grow back quicker than you'd think. Keep a pocketful and you're never far from all right.

**`iona_hearth__cook`** — *follows straight on from "forage"*

> Now the proper lesson. Take these, raw chicken, and hold them to my fire. Stand at the flames and cook. You'll know it's done by the smell. Every campfire in the world works the same as this one.

**`iona_hearth__burn`** — *follows straight on from "cook"*

> You'll likely burn the first one. Everyone does. The fire takes one as its fee. The second you'll eat. Off you go, and come see me whenever the pot's on.

**`iona_hearth__hub`** — *follows straight on from "burn"; or follows straight on from "where"*

> Anything else, love?

**`iona_hearth__where`** — *player says: "Where were those berries again?"*

> South of the bridge, along the near bank. Berries, and the tall fibre plants. Fen the tinker wants those for twine. And sageroot, which any healer will thank you for. Take what you pass.

**`iona_hearth__farewell`** — *player says: "Thanks, Iona. That's plenty."*

> Get a meal in you before the yard, and a night's sleep before the road. Off you go now.

### Conversation: `q_the_pot_never_rests_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_pot_never_rests:available)*

**`q_the_pot_never_rests_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Pot's low and the brook's generous. Six trout, if your rod's willing. The fish bite where the water sounds busiest. There'll be a bowl in it for you. There always is.

**`q_the_pot_never_rests_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Six trout, coming up."*

> Take bread for the bank. Fishing's hungry work, whatever it looks like.

**`q_the_pot_never_rests_offer__declined`** — *player says: "No time to fish today."*

> Then come by for a bowl anyway.

### Conversation: `q_the_pot_never_rests_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_pot_never_rests:ready)*

**`q_the_pot_never_rests_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six good ones. Into the pot they go. And these two are yours, cooked proper. You've earned a supper you didn't catch.

## Tinker Fen `tinker_fen` — 7 dialogue lines, 15 quips and barks

*Half the village is held together by things Fen made from the other half.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Village tinker, a little lonely, happiest mid-repair. Talks to tools and objects mid-sentence ('hold still, you...'). ### Conversation: `fen_bench`

**`fen_bench__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or player says: "Something else."; or follows straight on from "boards"*

> Hold still, you... no, not you, the vice. It slips. Fen. Tinker, whittler, mender of latches nobody thanks me for. You've the look of somebody who wants to MAKE something. Am I right?

**`fen_bench__make`** — *player says: "What can I make out here?"*

> This workbench answers to anyone. Bring it logs from the axe, hides from the hunt, ore from the pick. It'll show you what your hands can shape. Iona's fire does the food; my bench does the rest. You could walk out of this village wearing nothing you didn't make yourself. I have. This shirt's older than Pip.

**`fen_bench__boards`** — *player says: "And if I want to build a house?"*

> A wall wants boards, not whole trunks... hold the... there. Two logs make a sawhorse; the sawhorse makes any log three boards. Raise one where you fell timber, stack the boards flat, walk home light. Mine's just past the crate. The trees never... well. They never carry themselves.

**`fen_bench__decor`** — *player says: "And who hangs a sign for me?"*

> Nobody. You do. A banner off a rod, a trade board on its bracket, canvas over a window if the sun sits wrong... any wall you can touch will carry it. The dye you steep yourself. Berries do a red, moonbell does the blue that... hm. The blue. Take it down and the wall hands most of it back.

**`fen_bench__grow`** — *player says: "Where does a crafter go to grow?"*

> Out there? Better benches in stranger places: old forges in ruins, waystation kits, whatever you raise with your own hands. And watch for recipe scrolls. Read one and your hands keep it forever. Chests carry them. So do the pockets of things that... hm. Things you'll have to argue with first.

**`fen_bench__twine`** — *player says: "What's with all the twine?"*

> Twine! Twine is... hand me that... thank you. Fibre plant, down by the brook. Twist it, and bows have strings, hooks have lines, and my winter repairs hold.

**`fen_bench__farewell`** — *player says: "Another time, Fen."*

> Bench is here when the urge takes you. Now hold still, you...

*The village's whole militia, and enough of one.*

### Conversation: `bryn_arms`

**`bryn_arms__size_up`** — *opens the conversation*

> Off the stones this morning, were you. Shoulders back. Better. I'm Bryn. I keep the peace here. Open your pack: the village put three weapons in it. I'll teach you all three. Won't take long.

**`bryn_arms__melee`** — *follows straight on from "size_up"; or player says: "The sword again."*

> First. The bronze sword. Equip it, get close, swing. One cut calls the next. The third lands hardest, so stay in and finish. When something swings back at you, dash. Quick step, any direction. Feet first. Guard second.

**`bryn_arms__ranged`** — *follows straight on from "melee"; or player says: "The bow again."*

> Second. The shortbow. Don't tap at it. Draw and hold. The longer the pull, the harder it hits. Loose early and you've wasted it. Full pull. Then let go. You'll feel the difference.

**`bryn_arms__magic`** — *follows straight on from "ranged"; or player says: "The staff again."*

> Third. The staff. Throws a spark. Your arm doesn't matter, your aim does. The schools teach you more tricks as they warm to you; that part minds itself. Blade, bow, spark. Learn all three. Favour one.

**`bryn_arms__hub`** — *follows straight on from "magic"*

> Again? Or ready for something that bites back?

**`bryn_arms__task`** — *player says: "Give me a real task."*

> The old shed across the ford, south-east, past the berry bushes. Rats in it the size of my fist. Wade the shallows, clear it out, and try each weapon while you're at it. There's an old traveller's chest in there too. Whatever it holds is yours. Report back when the shed goes quiet.

### Conversation: `bryn_watch_relief` *(plays when: world:relief)*

**`bryn_watch_relief__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "someone"*

> Fires came up one short last night. The right kind of short. Word says that was you.

**`bryn_watch_relief__praise`** — *player says: "It was."*

> Good. Rack your blade, eat something, sleep behind a door. That's an order.

**`bryn_watch_relief__someone`** — *player says: "Wasn't me."*

> Then somebody out there has my thanks and doesn't know it. Enjoy their quiet anyway.

**`bryn_watch_relief__pass`** — *player says: "Just passing the yard."*

> Pass through, then. It's a good day for it.

### Conversation: `bryn_watch_uneasy` *(plays when: world:threat_near)*

**`bryn_watch_uneasy__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "count"*

> Smoke past the hedgerows that isn't ours. I count fires at dusk. Last night there was one too many.

**`bryn_watch_uneasy__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked. Go before they dig in. Break it, come home, report.

**`bryn_watch_uneasy__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

> Same smoke as before. Your chart holds it. Go.

**`bryn_watch_uneasy__count`** — *player says: "How bad is it?"*

> Wolves take a lamb, that's weather. A camp takes the road, and the road is how bread gets here. Bad enough.

**`bryn_watch_uneasy__dismiss`** — *player says: "Not my errand today."*

> Then send me someone who will.

### Conversation: `bryn_watch_urgent` *(plays when: world:threat_bold)*

**`bryn_watch_urgent__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "noone"*

> They've stopped hiding their fires. That means numbers. Numbers mean they're deciding something.

**`bryn_watch_urgent__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked on your chart. Don't scout it. End it.

**`bryn_watch_urgent__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

> Camp hasn't moved. Their nerve has. The mark stands. Go.

**`bryn_watch_urgent__noone`** — *player says: "What if no one goes?"*

> Then they get bolder. Then they come down the road. I've seen the order it happens in.

**`bryn_watch_urgent__hold`** — *player says: "Hold the yard."*

> Always.

### Conversation: `bryn_yard`

**`bryn_yard__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "recap"; or follows straight on from "praise"*

> Yard's open. Speak.

**`bryn_yard__recap`** — *player says: "Remind me of the three schools."*

> Sword: three cuts, third lands hardest, dash what you can't trade. Bow: full draw or don't bother. Staff: aim, the spark does the rest. That's the drill. Now go use it.

**`bryn_yard__praise`** — *player says: "The shed's gone quiet. Rats are down."*

> So it HAS gone quiet. Well cut, waker. You opened the chest too, I hope. Never leave a chest shut. Here: arrow, thirty of them. That's as near a medal as this village gives. When Rowan sends you east, you'll do.

**`bryn_yard__beyond`** — *player says: "What's out past the hedgerows?"*

> Inside the hedgerows, nothing will touch you. Past them it gets braver by the mile: stray wolves first, then camps with watch-fires, and out where the maps give up, things with names. The wayfarers' lanterns are the only friendly lights out there. Mind your distance.

**`bryn_yard__dismiss`** — *player says: "Just passing the yard."*

> Then pass through. Mind the racks.

### Conversation: `q_thin_the_meadow_offer` *(plays when: quest:thin_the_meadow:available)*

**`q_thin_the_meadow_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Tracks in the south meadow. Goblin. Three mornings running, closer each day. I want six of them down before they decide my hedgerows look soft. Yours?

**`q_thin_the_meadow_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Consider it done."*

> Good. South, past the lane. Count them out loud if it helps. It helps me.

**`q_thin_the_meadow_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not my fight."*

> It will be. Come back when you've noticed.

### Conversation: `q_thin_the_meadow_turnin` *(plays when: quest:thin_the_meadow:ready)*

**`q_thin_the_meadow_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six. I counted. Well cut, waker. Here's the yard's thanks, and my better mood, which is rarer.

*Ink-stained fingers, a banker's stoop, and the calm of a man who has counted everything he owns twice.*

- `banker_cormund__bark_1` — "The vault is stone, the ledger is ink, and both outlast a promise."
- `banker_cormund__bark_2` — "My father kept the ford toll in a wooden box. The year the Redmasks chained the ford, the box taught us all a lesson. The bank is that lesson, in stone."
- `banker_cormund__bark_3` — "Bursar Odele of Silverfall countersigns our charter. Her letters arrive with every caravan and never run past a page."

### Conversation: `cormund_ledger`

**`cormund_ledger__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome to the Amberford bank. Deposits at the counter, withdrawals at the counter, and the vault behind me holds both.

**`cormund_ledger__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "how"; or follows straight on from "toll"*

> How may the bank serve?

**`cormund_ledger__how`** — *player says: "How does banking work, exactly?"*

> Use the bank chests, one by each rug. What you put in is yours, recorded twice, and reachable from any bank chest in any town. Coin in a ledger travels faster than coin in a pocket, and is considerably harder to stab. The service is free.

**`cormund_ledger__toll`** — *player says: "Why does a ford town have a bank?"*

> My father kept the ford toll in a wooden box with a wooden lock. The autumn the Redmasks chained the ford, they walked off with it, box and all. Captain Aldis broke the chain. I built the vault. Between us, it has not happened twice.

**`cormund_ledger__odele`** — *player says: "Silverfall countersigns your charter?"*

> Bursar Odele, of the Bank of Silverfall. Every charter bank on the two roads clears through her vault row. Her letters arrive with each caravan. Terse. Exact. I have kept every one.

**`cormund_ledger__bye`** — *player says: "That's all, thank you."*

> Good day. The counter is here when you need it.

### Conversation: `q_the_stolen_ledger_active` *(plays when: quest:the_stolen_ledger:active)*

**`q_the_stolen_ledger_active__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> A torn page finds its way home. Bank rule, my clerk's hand, and a Redmask thumb on the margin.

**`q_the_stolen_ledger_active__ask`** — *follows straight on from "hub"*

> The column they took is still owed. Collect five of the band that held it, and the bank will remember being owed to you. We're very good at remembering.

**`q_the_stolen_ledger_active__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll collect it."; or player says: "Just returning what I found."*

> The marches, where the fires burn cold. Mind the arithmetic: five.

### Conversation: `q_the_stolen_ledger_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_stolen_ledger:ready)*

**`q_the_stolen_ledger_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Five, off the road's ledger and onto mine. I said the bank remembers. Here's yours, with interest. My door knows your name now.

### Conversation: `aldis_fine` *(plays when: faction:fordgate:atmost:outlaw)*

**`aldis_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> Stop there. Your name's in the bad column, and the gate doesn't serve that column. The book sets a price: coin against the harm done.

**`aldis_fine__quote`** — *player says: "How much?"*

> She runs a finger down the column.

**`aldis_fine__pay`** — *player says: "I'll pay it."*

> She opens the strongbox and waits.

**`aldis_fine__bye`** — *player says: "Not today."*

> Then walk wide of my gate.

### Conversation: `aldis_gate`

**`aldis_gate__truth`** — *opens the conversation*

> Hold up. New face at the north gate gets the speech. This wall is where the settled land ends. Every mile north is meaner than the last. Goblins in the foothills. Wolves under the Thornveil. Past the Last Lamp, worse. I won't name it at a gate.

**`aldis_gate__ask`** — *follows straight on from "truth"*

> The Waykeepers hold three walled lamps on the way north: Fernway, the Long Meadow, the Fork. Walk lamp to lamp. Sleep behind their walls. The day the road starts feeling interested in you, turn around. That's the speech.

**`aldis_gate__heeded`** — *player says: "Understood, Captain. Lamp to lamp."*

> Good. See Hask, the outfitter across the way, before you go. Get your boots looked at. Road keep you.

**`aldis_gate__shrugged`** — *player says: "I can handle the road."*

> Mm. They all say that. I'll keep a page free in the incident book. Prove me wrong.

### Conversation: `aldis_good_column` *(plays when: faction:fordgate:atleast:trusted)*

**`aldis_good_column__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "work"*

> Gate's quiet. Your name's in the good column. The watch reads that book every shift.

**`aldis_good_column__work`** — *player says: "Anything need doing?"*

> My rounds are covered. Folk with work to give carry a mark over their heads. Go and ask.

**`aldis_good_column__bye`** — *player says: "Just passing, Captain."*

> Pass. You don't need checking.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_heeded` *(plays when: aldis_heeded)*

**`aldis_watch_heeded__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "road"; or follows straight on from "toll"*

> Still walking lamp to lamp? Good. What do you need?

**`aldis_watch_heeded__road`** — *player says: "How's the road today?"*

> Quiet to the Meadow. Redmask sign on the middle stretch. And the Fork tower lit its brazier at the wrong hour twice this week. Could be nothing. If you pass the wardens' outpost, tell the sergeant I want her count.

**`aldis_watch_heeded__toll`** — *player says: "What was the Toll War?"*

> Before the bank, the ford toll sat in a wooden box. One autumn the Redmasks chained the ford and taxed this town at its own crossing. Three days. On the fourth we went out and took the chain down. It cost us the names on the pillar by the bank. Read them when you pass. The chain itself sits in Cormund's vault. He'll show you, if you ask him straight.

**`aldis_watch_heeded__bye`** — *player says: "Carry on, Captain."*

> Road keep you. Mind the lamps.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_list` *(plays when: faction:fordgate:suspect)*

**`aldis_watch_list__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "count"*

> You're on the watch-list. Not my doing. You put your own name in that column.

**`aldis_watch_list__count`** — *player says: "Is that a threat?"*

> It's a count. We count everything that comes through this gate. Keep clean and we've no quarrel.

**`aldis_watch_list__bye`** — *player says: "I'll mind myself."*

> Do that. The book stays open.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_relief` *(plays when: world:relief)*

**`aldis_watch_relief__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quiet"*

> The book got a good entry for once: camp broken, road open. By all accounts, your doing.

**`aldis_watch_relief__thanks`** — *player says: "The road's yours again."*

> It's the town's road. The town breathes easier tonight. I've logged the deed under your name.

**`aldis_watch_relief__quiet`** — *player says: "Anything else stirring?"*

> Quiet, for now. I know better than to trust it. I'll take it anyway.

**`aldis_watch_relief__salute`** — *player says: "Captain."*

> Waker.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_toll` *(plays when: world:toll_near)*

**`aldis_watch_toll__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "war"*

> There's a bar across my road and it isn't mine. They're charging for the crossing. A toll. I don't say that word lightly in this town.

**`aldis_watch_toll__mark`** — *player says: "Where's the toll?"*

> Marked. Break the bar, or break the camp that feeds it. Either way my road opens.

**`aldis_watch_toll__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

> The mark stands. So does the bar. See to it.

**`aldis_watch_toll__war`** — *player says: "Like the war?"*

> The Redmasks chained the ford once. It cost this town names we still read at dusk. I was made at that gate. I won't stand for a second plaque.

**`aldis_watch_toll__bye`** — *player says: "I'll see to it."*

> Then go. The gate stays open for your return.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_uneasy` *(plays when: world:threat_near)*

**`aldis_watch_uneasy__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "serious"*

> New entry in the incident book: camp sign off the road. Fresh, orderly, wrong side of my gate.

**`aldis_watch_uneasy__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked. The log will say I sent you.

**`aldis_watch_uneasy__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

> Check your chart. It hasn't moved. Neither have they.

**`aldis_watch_uneasy__serious`** — *player says: "How serious?"*

> I've doubled the watch and I bar the gate at dusk now. That's my answer.

**`aldis_watch_uneasy__bye`** — *player says: "Carry on, Captain."*

> Mind the road.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_urgent` *(plays when: world:threat_bold)*

**`aldis_watch_urgent__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "toll"*

> The camp has grown. My book calls that a muster. I don't have the spears to answer it.

**`aldis_watch_urgent__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked. Break the camp and I'll log it under your name.

**`aldis_watch_urgent__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

> The mark's still on your chart. Go soon. They're growing.

**`aldis_watch_urgent__toll`** — *player says: "What's this about a toll?"*

> They've put a bar across my road and they're charging for the crossing. The Redmasks did the same in the war. I was at this gate when the names went on the plaque. Break the toll or break the camp that feeds it. Either one ends both.

**`aldis_watch_urgent__bye`** — *player says: "Carry on, Captain."*

> Mind the road. I mean it more than usual.

### Conversation: `aldis_watch_wry` *(plays when: aldis_shrugged)*

**`aldis_watch_wry__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "relent"; or follows straight on from "road"*

> Still upright, then. The incident book waits. What?

**`aldis_watch_wry__relent`** — *player says: "Fine, tell me about the lamps."*

> Ha. There it is. Fernway, the Long Meadow, the Fork. Walk lamp to lamp and sleep behind walls. Past Edda's light at the Last Lamp, go armed, fed, and rested. Took you long enough.

**`aldis_watch_wry__road`** — *player says: "How's the road today?"*

> Meaner than last week. Redmask sign on the middle stretch again. Want particulars? Buy a bowl at Dunna's and listen to whichever table talks quietest.

**`aldis_watch_wry__bye`** — *player says: "Carry on, Captain."*

> Stay out of my incident book.

### Conversation: `q_the_bad_column_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_bad_column:available)*

**`q_the_bad_column_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Your name's in the bad column. Sorry doesn't move ink. Work does. Redmasks on the roads out from the ford. Five off their count.

**`q_the_bad_column_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll do the work."*

> Then the book waits. Come back when the count says five.

**`q_the_bad_column_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not that kind of work."*

> Then the column stands as written.

### Conversation: `q_the_bad_column_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_bad_column:ready)*

**`q_the_bad_column_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Five, confirmed by the road wardens. The book moves your name. Keep it moving the right way.

### Conversation: `q_the_lay_of_the_land_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_lay_of_the_land:ready)*

**`q_the_lay_of_the_land_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> In off the west road, alone, standing straight. Rowan's mark, that. She still sends me the ones worth the walk. Amberford's yours to learn, waker. Gate stays open till the horn says otherwise.

### Conversation: `q_the_reavers_mark_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_reavers_mark:available)*

**`q_the_reavers_mark_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Every band answers to a reaver, the one who keeps the shares. Break the biggest camp standing and take his mark. Then carry it past me, to Ansel at the Waykeepers' Hall. The registry outlives my temper. Will you do it?

**`q_the_reavers_mark_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "How will I know him?"*

> By the coat, and by everyone else standing behind him. Find the camp with a name in it. Mind the archers.

**`q_the_reavers_mark_offer__declined`** — *player says: "That's above my head."*

> Then it keeps. Reavers always do.

### Conversation: `q_word_on_the_road_offer` *(plays when: quest:word_on_the_road:available)*

**`q_word_on_the_road_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You came in off the roads, so you saw it: cold fires, cut fences. Bands working the marches again. I want four of them down, and I don't much mind which four. Take the work?

**`q_word_on_the_road_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Where do I find them?"*

> Camps drift. Ask the watch what stands near, or walk until the grass goes burned. That's their country. Report when it's four.

**`q_word_on_the_road_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not today, Captain."*

> Then keep to the walls after dusk. That's not a figure of speech.

### Conversation: `q_word_on_the_road_turnin` *(plays when: quest:word_on_the_road:ready)*

**`q_word_on_the_road_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Four down, and writs to prove whose. Redmask hand. I'd know it asleep. That name built this gate, and filled a plaque doing it. Good work. I don't say that to be kind.

> Anything else, love?

**`merra_market__cape`** — *player says: "Whose cape is that on the wall?"*

> My Edwin's. Wayfarer, caravan guard, best whistler on two roads. He walked north the spring the wolves came down early, and the road kept him. Keeper Ansel has his name in the hall registry. I keep the cape.

**`merra_market__cape2`** — *player says: "I'm sorry."; or player says: "(Say nothing, and let the shop be quiet a moment.)"*

> None of that, now. Fifteen good years he gave me, and a clean cape at the end. Most get less. Now buy something, love, before I get weepy.

**`merra_market__tilo`** — *player says: "Tell me about your brother."*

> Tilo? Cleverest hands in town, and not a lick of sense to go with them. He built every shelf in this shop in one week, then he spent three years not finishing a chair. That's my brother.

**`merra_market__nib`** — *player says: "You feed the courier girl, I hear."*

**`merra_market__browse`** — *player says: "Let me see the shelves."*

### Conversation: `dunna_hearthfire` *(plays when: dlg:dunna_rest)*

**`dunna_hearthfire__sniff`** — *opens the conversation*

> Smell that? Yard fire's going. Midday I do the stew out there. The indoor hearth keeps you warm, love. The yard fire does the cooking.

**`dunna_hearthfire__offer`** — *follows straight on from "sniff"*

> Here's the arrangement, same as I give every waker: the yard fire is yours whenever it's lit. Catch a trout off Peld's dock, cook it on my coals, no charge. Peld keeps his own fire down the shore, if you'd rather smell like the pond. And when you're tired of your own cooking, the board's right here.

**`dunna_hearthfire__teach`** — *player says: "What should I learn to cook first?"*

**`dunna_hearthfire__board`** — *player says: "Let's see the board, Dunna."*

### Conversation: `dunna_rest`

**`dunna_rest__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome to the Wanderer's Rest. Beds, board, and news. Stew's on.

**`dunna_rest__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "peddler"; or follows straight on from "osa"*

> What'll you have?

**`dunna_rest__news`** — *player says: "Give me the news, then."; or follows straight on from "seal"; or follows straight on from "roads"*

> Pick your poison.

**`dunna_rest__peddler`** — *player says: "Anything worth chasing?"*

> A peddler's cart went by at dawn, bells and all, and parked somewhere up the road. Carts don't wait, love. Best hurry.

**`dunna_rest__seal`** — *player says: "What's this about the mountain?"*

> The big one: Silverfall's Masons broke the Undercroft seal. Twenty years shut, and now there's a market down there again. Kobolds past the rubble line too, which folk say quieter. Every stool in this room has an opinion on it. Ask Bretta at the forge. She's mountain-born. She was there.

**`dunna_rest__roads`** — *player says: "How are the roads running?"*

> First Road's tame: hedgerows, wayshrines, the odd goblin scout getting above himself. The High Road is another matter. Fine to the Long Meadow, chancy to the Fork, and past Edda's lamp you'd best be serious about yourself. The Redmasks work the middle stretch. Travel mornings, and travel loud.

**`dunna_rest__strange`** — *player says: "Anything strange lately?"*

> Peld swears something big turned over in the millpond, twice last month. Garton swears it was Peld's own bell. Perl swears her cows have learnt to open the gate, and I believe Perl. Small town. The strange here stays friendly.

**`dunna_rest__osa`** — *player says: "Your mother kept this bar before you?"*

> Mam ran this room thirty years. Osa. Ask anyone grey enough. When my father passed she couldn't sit still in this room, so she kissed the bar and walked the High Road at sixty. Now she waters caravan mules under Silverfall's wall, and writes once a season to say my stew wants more thyme. She's right. Don't you dare tell her.

**`dunna_rest__browse`** — *player says: "What's good tonight?"*

> Stew, bread, roast, and cake. Sit. Eat. The road can wait an hour.

**`dunna_rest__fire`** — *player says: "Just the fire, thanks."*

> Fire's free. Sit as long as you like.

### Conversation: `hask_roadgear`

**`hask_roadgear__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Stop. Boots. Mm. They'll do to the Long Meadow. Past that, we should talk. Hask. Outfitter, fletcher. Last shop before the High Road.

**`hask_roadgear__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "kit"; or follows straight on from "waykeeper"*

> Speak your business.

**`hask_roadgear__kit`** — *player says: "What does the road ask for?"*

> Arrows, double what you brought. A snare kit, so dinner doesn't cost steel. Spare bowstring. Dry socks. And be under a roof by nightfall. Most that die out there went out underprepared.

**`hask_roadgear__waykeeper`** — *player says: "You were a Waykeeper?"*

> Fifteen years. Escort sergeant, Amberford to the Last Lamp and back, more times than I've got teeth left. Retired the winter the worgs came down on the Fork rest and took two of mine inside the fence line. I keep their names off my tongue.

**`hask_roadgear__aldis`** — *player says: "Captain Aldis trained under you?"*

> Best cadet I ever shouted at. Only one who ever shouted back and was right. When the Toll War broke, she's the one who went out on the ice and broke the Redmask chain with a mattock. The town gave her the gate the same week.

**`hask_roadgear__browse`** — *player says: "Kit me out."*

> Racks are yours. Buy for the road you're actually walking.

### Conversation: `q_pelts_for_the_road_offer` *(plays when: quest:pelts_for_the_road:available)*

**`q_pelts_for_the_road_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Winter cloaks want lining and I won't sell thin. Six wolf furs, clean ones. Wolves run the tree lines, and they don't come alone. Hear that part twice. Work you want?

**`q_pelts_for_the_road_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Six furs. Done."*

> Aim before the second one commits. Off you go.

**`q_pelts_for_the_road_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not for wolf pay."*

> Fair enough.

### Conversation: `q_pelts_for_the_road_turnin` *(plays when: quest:pelts_for_the_road:ready)*

**`q_pelts_for_the_road_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six, and clean. Somebody taught you skinning, or you listened the first time. Three cloaks lined, one road-death fewer this winter, the way I count it.

### Conversation: `q_the_matriarch_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_matriarch:available)*

**`q_the_matriarch_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> I'm going to say a thing I've only said twice, and I restocked for both of them after. There's a den in the deep wood off the hunter's trail. A matriarch runs it: dire, old, and every pack for miles answers her.

**`q_the_matriarch_offer__two`** — *player says: "What happened to the other two?"*

> One's lying in front of the den. The other doesn't hunt anymore. Know that before you say yes.

**`q_the_matriarch_offer__dead`** — *player says: "You want her dead."; or player says: "I'll pay it. She dies."*

> Break the packs between you and the den first, or you fight all of them at her door. Then her. Bring the pelt whole, not for coin. I'll work it into something worth what it cost.

**`q_the_matriarch_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I like my straps and my life."*

> That's the answer that keeps my restock bill down. Offer stands.

### Conversation: `q_the_matriarch_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_matriarch:ready)*

**`q_the_matriarch_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> direwolf pelt Whole. You brought it whole.

**`q_the_matriarch_turnin__targe`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> The targe is wolfjaw work: her kin's own teeth set in the rim. Carry it and the packs will smell what it is. Some will think twice. The stupid ones won't, but that's what the targe is for.

**`q_the_matriarch_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "targe"*

> The traveler in front of the den can rest now. I'll see someone goes for him before the snow. Good work.

### Conversation: `q_worgsong_offer` *(plays when: quest:worgsong:available)*

**`q_worgsong_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Your straps are holding. Good. Ready for the bigger cousins? Worgs are running with the packs northwest. A worg fang goes through cheap leather like wet paper, and I want four for buckle-work.

**`q_worgsong_offer__find`** — *player says: "How do I find them?"*

> You won't. They find you. That's the song. You'll hear it start behind you and finish in front. Keep your back to a rock and swing at the second howl, not the first.

**`q_worgsong_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Four fangs. Done."; or player says: "Noted. I'm going."*

> Thin the runners, take four good fangs. There's a snare kit in it, my own build.

**`q_worgsong_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not yet."*

> Fair. The song's not going anywhere.

### Conversation: `q_worgsong_turnin` *(plays when: quest:worgsong:ready)*

**`q_worgsong_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Four fangs, no cracks, and you're standing square on both legs. That's the whole inspection. These'll buckle a strap a bear couldn't open. Kit's yours, coin's yours. And that look you're wearing: everyone comes back from the song with it.

### Conversation: `bretta_delf` *(plays when: dlg:bretta_forge)*

**`bretta_delf__look`** — *opens the conversation*

> Back again. Good. The ones who come back are worth teaching. Before you buy a single schematic off me, answer this. Where does a bar of bronze start?

**`bretta_delf__wrong`** — *player says: "At the furnace?"*

> No. Furnace is the middle. It starts in the ground. North spine past Hask's, dirt trail east at the lamp: that's the Amber Delf, the old cutting. Copper in the west face. Tin in the floor. I'm up there at first light most mornings. An hour of swinging feeds this forge for a day.

**`bretta_delf__right`** — *player says: "In the ground."*

> In the ground. Ha. There's hope for you. North spine past Hask's, dirt trail east at the lamp: the Amber Delf, the old cutting. Copper in the west face. Tin in the floor. I'm up there at first light most mornings. An hour of swinging feeds this forge for a day.

**`bretta_delf__lesson`** — *follows straight on from "wrong"; or follows straight on from "right"*

> Your ladder, free of charge: dig copper and tin. Smelt bronze at my furnace. Hammer it on the spare anvil till your arms understand. And when you hit the north face, the gray one that laughs at bronze picks, that's iron. Iron wants a better pick. A better pick wants a better smith.

**`bretta_delf__sell`** — *player says: "Show me your schematics, then."*

> Thought you'd never ask. Priced at what they'll earn you back twice over.

**`bretta_delf__send`** — *player says: "I'll go find the Delf first."*

> Better answer than the schematics. Go. And mind Holloway's cows on the way past.

### Conversation: `bretta_forge`

**`bretta_forge__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "teach"; or follows straight on from "busy"*

> Forge's hot. Speak.

**`bretta_forge__teach`** — *player says: "Teach me smithing."*

> Scrolls on my shelf. Every pattern the guilds teach, jewellery to plate. Buy the one your hands are ready for, no higher. The metal will tell you if you've flattered yourself. Copper and tin first. Everyone starts at copper and tin.

**`bretta_forge__busy`** — *player says: "How does a ford town keep a master smith busy?"*

> Two roads' worth of horseshoes. A bank's worth of hinges. Every plough blade from here to the hedgerows. And lately, arrowheads. More than I like. Hask doubled his order last month.

**`bretta_forge__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the schematics."*

> Take your time. The steel's not going anywhere.

**`bretta_forge__warm`** — *player says: "Just warming my hands."*

> That's what the fire's for. Warm them, then put them to work.

### Conversation: `bretta_mountain`

**`bretta_mountain__news`** — *opens the conversation*

> You'll have heard what the caravans are shouting. The Masons' Guild broke their own seal. The Undercroft is open again. Twenty years shut. Open again.

**`bretta_mountain__father`** — *follows straight on from "news"*

> I swung my first hammer down there, under the mountain. Grand Forge apprentice, me and Balla, fighting over the same anvil. Then the kobolds came up through the deep galleries, and the Guild closed the whole district. My father's crew set the last stones of the seal. He set stone the way I set edges. Properly. The seal was his.

**`bretta_mountain__choice`** — *follows straight on from "father"*

> So when the coal boys sing about open galleries, I hear a door my father built, propped open with his own chisel. That's all the story I've got. What do you want at my forge?

**`bretta_mountain__back`** — *player says: "Would you ever go back up?"*

> Balla's asked. Every solstice letter, one line at the bottom: the anvil's still here. Maybe now the door's open I'll walk up and lose the trials to her again. Once. For the look on her face. If you pass the Grand Forge before I do, tell her Bretta says her quenches always ran cold.

**`bretta_mountain__sorry`** — *player says: "I'm sorry about your father."*

> So am I. Twenty years' practice at it now. He'd have liked this town, I think. He always said stone should hold something: coin, bread, people. This one holds all three.

**`bretta_mountain__browse`** — *player says: "Show me what you sell."*

> Schematics on the shelf, steel on the racks. Priced honest. I can't be bothered to haggle.

**`bretta_mountain__end`** — *follows straight on from "back"; or follows straight on from "sorry"*

> Right. Enough smoke without a fire under it. Come by when you need steel, or the knowing of it.

### Conversation: `q_a_smiths_errand_offer` *(plays when: quest:a_smiths_errand:available)*

**`q_a_smiths_errand_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Forge's hot. Yard's slow. Six iron, four coal. Seams east of the ford if you swing a pick, Merra's counter if you don't. Fetching?

**`q_a_smiths_errand_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll fetch it."*

> Good. Ore first. Talk after.

**`q_a_smiths_errand_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find another back."*

> Suit yourself. Forge won't.

**`q_a_smiths_errand_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Weighed true. That'll pour clean. You fetch like someone who's worked. Take the wage.

*Boots older than most fences, and a voice she saves for animals. The stalls behind her are swept twice a day, and not for your sake.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeps the stalls behind the green. Boots older than most fences, and a voice she saves for animals. Speaks to you the way she speaks to a nervous horse: low, unhurried, no sudden words. Orders disguised as observations.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

### Conversation: `drover_stalls`

**`drover_stalls__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Hold. Let them smell you first. Right. Now we can talk.

**`drover_stalls__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "words"; or follows straight on from "pen"*

> What is it, then?

**`drover_stalls__words`** — *player says: "Is the asking all there is?"*

> No. The asking is the first word of a long tongue. A hush for a riled heart. A whistle that folds the road. A howl you share with your friend. They come to your hands as your hands earn them. Steady. Steady, I said. Not you.

**`drover_stalls__pen`** — *player says: "What is this pen for?"*

> Three stalls to a household, one friend at your heel. Swap them here. Rest one that limped home. And when a bond has run its course, this is where you slip the collar.

**`drover_stalls__gentle`** — *player says: "How do you gentle a wild thing?"*

> It is a working now, the old drovers' asking. Learn it when your hands know beasts well enough, and keep it ready. Call the beast, hold your ground, and carry what it wants in your pack. It will come at you the whole while. Stand through it.

**`drover_stalls__teeth`** — *player says: "It keeps attacking you?"*

> The wild does not shake hands. Easy now. Yes, the whole while. Wear its fight down first and the asking is half as long. Or stand there whole and eat every bite. Your choice, your hide.

**`drover_stalls__lure`** — *player says: "What do they want?"*

> Depends on the belly. Beetles come for berries. A rat wants an egg, whole, no cracks. Ask Hobb, he farms by the pasture, what the rats take already.

**`drover_stalls__simple`** — *player says: "Sounds simple."*

> Standing still is simple too and people still flinch. Move a foot and the asking breaks. Bears are not simple. Plant yourself where you mean to stay.

**`drover_stalls__own`** — *player says: "Do you keep one yourself?"*

> Kept droves forty years. People call hunters cruel, but a hunting beast is spoken to all day. A yard beast is counted. I know which one comes when I whistle.

**`drover_stalls__off`** — *player says: "That's all."*

> Gate on your way out. They notice.

# The roads — waystations, watch and the Tollhouse

## Ferrick `company_broker` — 21 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*He sits like a man who owns the road and rents it back by the mile. The ledger open in front of him has two columns and no headings.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Ferrick, the Company's Tongue at the Tollhouse. Courteous menace; never raises his voice, never threatens twice. Everything is a ledger entry, everyone an amount. A clerk's dry wit, spent sparingly. Smooth, unhurried, faintly amused.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/veil_ethan` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.603

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `company_broker__bark_1` — "The road was here before the towns. The Company just collects what it's owed."
- `company_broker__bark_2` — "Sit, if you're sitting. Stand there, if you like being counted."
- `company_broker__bark_3` — "Every cart that passes pays somebody. The only question is who."

### Conversation: `ferrick_court`

**`ferrick_court__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "who"; or follows straight on from "place"*

> Sit, if you like. The road was here before the towns, and the Company was here before the wardens. What do you want?

**`ferrick_court__who`** — *player says: "Who are you?"*

> Ferrick. I keep the Company's ledger for this stretch. Two columns, no headings: people who are useful, and people who owe. You get to pick your column.

**`ferrick_court__place`** — *player says: "What is this place?"*

> A tollhouse. The bar goes up for friends of the road and down for everyone else. The wardens hang lamps and call the road theirs. Lamps burn out. A debt doesn't.

**`ferrick_court__counter`** — *player says: "What do you buy and sell?"*

> Buying, and buying back. The Company's ledger runs both directions. Whatever arrives in your pack with a history stays off the page.

**`ferrick_court__bye`** — *player says: "Nothing from you."*

> Then you're paying in walking.

### Conversation: `ferrick_fine` *(plays when: faction:reavers:atmost:outlaw)*

**`ferrick_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> You've cost the Company blood, and the Company writes blood in coin. We're practical people. Settle the column and the road forgets you were ever bad business.

**`ferrick_fine__quote`** — *player says: "What's the blood-price?"*

> He turns the ledger so you can see the figure.

**`ferrick_fine__pay`** — *player says: "I'll settle it."*

> He clears a space on the table, unhurried.

**`ferrick_fine__bye`** — *player says: "The Company can keep its ledger."*

> It keeps itself. That's the trouble with ledgers.

### Conversation: `q_the_lean_winter_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_lean_winter:available)*

**`q_the_lean_winter_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Bigger work. The ford eats well, so the ford bargains badly. Four head of cattle off Amberford's pastures and the winter leans our way. The Charter will hate you for it. Count that in the wages.

**`q_the_lean_winter_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "The herd's as good as gone."*

> Quietly, if you can. Loudly will also do.

**`q_the_lean_winter_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I don't make war on cattle."*

> It's all somebody's herd. Suit your stomach.

### Conversation: `q_the_lean_winter_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_lean_winter:ready)*

**`q_the_lean_winter_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Four head. The ford will feel it by first frost, and feel who to thank a little after. Welcome to the better column.

### Conversation: `q_the_red_mark_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_red_mark:available)*

**`q_the_red_mark_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Small work first. Carry the Company's word to Calder, under the bank's shadow in Silverfall. He asks no questions. The ford's registry will mind, if it ever learns. That's the price of the better column.

**`q_the_red_mark_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."*

> The word is one sentence. Calder will know the shape of it.

**`q_the_red_mark_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not the Company's errand-hand."*

> Then you're cargo, not courier.

### Conversation: `q_the_red_mark_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_red_mark:ready)*

**`q_the_red_mark_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Landed clean. Calder's silence travels faster than most men's letters. Your name moves columns now.

### Conversation: `q_toll_owed_offer` *(plays when: quest:toll_owed:available)*

**`q_toll_owed_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Standing arrangement, for road-friends: a hundred and twenty coins, source unasked. Call it a toll on the road you walk anyway.

**`q_toll_owed_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll bring the cut."*

> The ledger stays open. It always does.

**`q_toll_owed_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Collect it yourself."*

> We do. Constantly. This was the polite version.

### Conversation: `q_toll_owed_turnin` *(plays when: quest:toll_owed:ready)*

**`q_toll_owed_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Counted once. The Company trusts road-friends to the coin. Your column improves.

## Edda `lampkeeper_edda` — 3 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Older than the road she keeps, by her own accounting. Lights four lamps at dusk in an order that never varies, and has buried everyone who asked why out of turn.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeper of the Last Lamp on the worst mile of road; Sella's elder sister. BLUNT. Shortest sentences in the game. Kindness lives in deeds, never words. No warmth in the voice; all the warmth is in what she does.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/dour_mabel` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.622 · cfg 0.603

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `lampkeeper_edda__bark_1` — "Advice? Morning. That's the whole of it. Everything north of my wall agrees with me."
- `lampkeeper_edda__bark_2` — "The bones outside the wall are the ones who went on at night. I light the lamps so the pile stops growing. It hasn't stopped. I keep lighting them."
- `lampkeeper_edda__bark_3` — "Silverfall's gate is a day out. The mountain doesn't mind you walking it. The dark between us minds very much."

### Conversation: `q_the_sisters_lamp_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_sisters_lamp:ready)*

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "word"*

## Sergeant Hale `waykeeper_hale` — 19 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Twenty years on the marches and a ledger of every camp broken and every mile held. Polishes the brazier like it outranks him.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Waykeeper sergeant far from relief. Report-speak, understatement, dark road humor kept short. 'The lamp stays lit' said like a password, not a poem. Tired but unbroken.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/edder` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.667 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `waykeeper_hale__bark_1` — "This post holds fourteen miles of road. Some days it holds them by one lamp and my mood."
- `waykeeper_hale__bark_2` — "Brigands ambush the toll bends. Wolves work the trail. Kobolds take the rest. Everyone's got a trade."
- `waykeeper_hale__bark_3` — "The one in the pen? Caught him stealing our boots. IN our boots."

### Conversation: `hale_post`

**`hale_post__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "holds"; or follows straight on from "doing"*

> Wardens' post. Fourteen miles of road and one lamp. What do you need?

**`hale_post__holds`** — *player says: "What holds the road?"*

> Us, the lamps, and the fences, in that order. Brigands hold the toll bends, wolves have the trail. I keep the ledger even.

**`hale_post__doing`** — *player says: "Anything need doing?"*

> Always. Tonight it's the same as every night: hold fourteen miles with six hands. When something's stirring out there, ask me and I'll point you at it.

**`hale_post__peddler`** — *player says: "Anything friendly out there?"*

> A cart with bells went up the road this morning and stopped. Friendly, by the ledger. Go quick. Carts don't keep.

**`hale_post__bye`** — *player says: "Hold the post."*

> That's the job.

### Conversation: `hale_watch_relief` *(plays when: world:relief)*

**`hale_watch_relief__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "word"*

> Ledger's clean this morning. The camp's gone. Burned out from the inside, the way I heard it. Your work?

**`hale_watch_relief__mine`** — *player says: "Mine."*

> Then the post owes you stew and silence. We're good for both.

**`hale_watch_relief__word`** — *player says: "Word travels fast out here."*

> Fourteen miles of it, faster than carts. Sit if you like.

**`hale_watch_relief__bye`** — *player says: "Keep the ledger clean."*

> Easier job today than yesterday. Thanks to somebody.

### Conversation: `hale_watch_uneasy` *(plays when: world:threat_near)*

**`hale_watch_uneasy__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "who"*

> Something's set up shop on my fourteen miles, uninvited. I keep a ledger of who works this road. They're not in it.

**`hale_watch_uneasy__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> There's your mark. The post can't leave the lamp, so the errand's yours.

**`hale_watch_uneasy__remark`** — *player says: "Say it again. Where?"*

> The mark's on your chart. It hasn't moved.

**`hale_watch_uneasy__who`** — *player says: "Who are they?"*

> Fires say brigand, tracks say more than four. Past that I'd be guessing.

**`hale_watch_uneasy__pass`** — *player says: "I'll pass."*

> Then walk the middle of the road and don't stop to look.

### Conversation: `hale_watch_urgent` *(plays when: world:threat_bold)*

**`hale_watch_urgent__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "hold"*

> It's grown. What was a camp is a garrison now, and garrisons don't pay toll, they charge it.

**`hale_watch_urgent__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked. Sergeant Odessa logs 'road holds' every dusk. Keep her honest.

**`hale_watch_urgent__remark`** — *player says: "Say it again. Where?"*

> Mark stands. So do they, last I looked.

**`hale_watch_urgent__hold`** — *player says: "Can the post hold?"*

> We hold the post. The road between posts I can't promise. That part's yours.

**`hale_watch_urgent__bye`** — *player says: "Lamp stays lit."*

> It does.

### Conversation: `wayward_road`

**`wayward_watch_relief__done`** — *player says: "It's done."*

**`wayward_watch_relief__sharp`** — *player says: "Stay sharp anyway."*

**`wayward_watch_relief__bye`** — *player says: "Enjoy the quiet."*

**`wayward_watch_uneasy__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "nights"*

> Fire's free, voice down. There's a camp out there we're watching instead of sleeping.

**`wayward_watch_uneasy__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

**`wayward_watch_uneasy__remark`** — *player says: "Say the bearing again."*

**`wayward_watch_uneasy__nights`** — *player says: "How long have they been there?"*

> That camp's done being shy. Drums past midnight now, and we count more of them than of us.

**`wayward_watch_urgent__mark`** — *player says: "Where are they camped?"*

> Marked. We'll hold the fire. You do the loud part.

**`wayward_watch_urgent__stay`** — *player says: "Should you fall back to town?"*

> And give them the mile? No. We stay.

**`wayward_watch_urgent__bye`** — *player says: "Hold the fire."*

> Lamp stays lit.

*All elbows, freckles, and forward motion. Her satchel has more patches than satchel, each one a story she'll sell you for a sweet.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Courier who wants to be everywhere already. All elbows, freckles and forward motion. Breathless, arrives mid-thought, leaves before finishing, knows everyone's business a day early. Fast; clip the ends of lines like she's already turning away.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `courier_nib__bark_2` — "Dunna gives me the box room, Merra gives me breakfast, Tilo made my satchel, and Captain Aldis gives me the LOOK. It's a good town."
- `courier_nib__bark_3` — "I know where everyone is at every hour. It's not magic, it's just legs."

### Conversation: `nib_streets`

**`nib_streets__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You're new! I know everyone, so I'd know. I'm Nib. Courier. Official. Mostly official. Message running, gate to gate, six sweeps a day, and I see EVERYTHING, which is my job and not nosiness, whatever Captain Aldis's face says.

**`nib_streets__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "where"; or follows straight on from "story"*

> What do you want to know? I know loads.

**`nib_streets__where`** — *player says: "Where is everyone this time of day?"*

> Mornings: Bretta's hammering, Merra's at her Round stall, Tamsin's in the fields, and Ansel's dusting the book. Midday: everyone eats. Inn if they're social, benches if they're Hask. Evenings: Garton watches his pond, Tilo sits on the chair-that-isn't-finished, and the Captain walks her wall. I could draw you a chart. I HAVE a chart.

**`nib_streets__story`** — *player says: "How'd you come to Amberford?"*

> Came in on a caravan when I was little. Fell asleep in the flour sacks at the back, woke up famous. Nobody came looking. Dunna said the box room was doing nothing anyway, Merra started 'accidentally' making too much breakfast, and Tilo made my satchel with my name burnt inside. So now I'm from here. Towns get to just DECIDE that, turns out. It's the best rule anywhere.

**`nib_streets__seen`** — *player says: "What have you seen today?"*

> Today? Two caravans in from the north gate talking about the mountain's cellar being open. The guards went all quiet-voiced about it, which means it's INTERESTING. Peld's bell rang itself at dawn again. And Perl's brindle cow was standing at the orchard gate just LOOKING at it. Working the latch out. I gave her a week.

**`nib_streets__bye`** — *player says: "Keep running, Nib."*

> Can't stop! If anyone asks, you didn't see which way I went!

### Conversation: `q_the_long_way_round_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_long_way_round:available)*

**`q_the_long_way_round_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You! You walk, don't you? Everyone walks. I've two roads in my legs today and there's a third: word for Hale at the west post, then the Silver Flagon, up the capital. Can you take it? Say yes fast.

**`q_the_long_way_round_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Yes. Slow down. Who first?"*

> Hale first. Waykeeper, west road, lamp's always lit. Then Ragna at the Flagon. Don't ask her anything, she hears enough. I owe you! Probably a secret!

**`q_the_long_way_round_offer__declined`** — *player says: "No. Breathe."*

> No time to be sad about it. Third road, here I come!

### Conversation: `q_the_long_way_round_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_long_way_round:ready)*

**`q_the_long_way_round_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> You're BACK! Hale signed, Ragna didn't blink. She never does. That's the whole route run and I didn't run it. Feels like a day off. I've heard of those. Wages! Real ones!

## Jorel Furrowfield `farmer_jorel` — 8 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Built like his own barn door. Soil under his nails that no scrubbing has ever fully argued with.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Half of the Furrowfield marriage; slow and deliberate where Tamsin is quick. His sentences arrive like carts, fully loaded and on time. Incomplete without her version of the same story.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/court_phil` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `farmer_jorel__bark_2` — "We crofted out past the hedges once, cousins to the Fernway folk. One bandit autumn cured us of the open country. I like a wall now."
- `farmer_jorel__bark_3` — "Tamsin plans the year, I dig it. Twenty seasons and neither of us has once wanted the other job."

### Conversation: `jorel_fields`

**`jorel_fields__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "croft"; or follows straight on from "crops"*

> Mind the furrows. What brings you out to the dirt?

**`jorel_fields__croft`** — *player says: "You weren't always town farmers, were you?"*

> We crofted out east once, past the hedges. Good soil. Bad neighbors. A bandit autumn came through and burnt the barn with the whole season in it. We watched from the treeline, holding the dog so he wouldn't bark. Tamsin's cousins still work the Fernway verges. Us, we came inside the walls. I don't regret it. I check the treeline some evenings, is all.

**`jorel_fields__crops`** — *player says: "What's growing this year?"*

> Wheat for Garton's wheel. Carrots for Merra's shelf. Cotton, if Tamsin gets her way. And she will. She's already talked to the soil behind my back. Everything this town eats starts in one of three places, and I'm standing on the biggest one. That's grand enough work for me.

**`jorel_fields__bye`** — *player says: "Just walking the fields."*

> Walk soft on the seed rows. The rest can take a boot.

### Conversation: `q_the_herd_stands_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_herd_stands:available)*

**`q_the_herd_stands_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Seen red cloth in the tree line twice this week. A farmer knows what watchers by a pasture want, and it isn't milk. Five of those Redmasks put down before they get bold, and my herd winters where it stands.

**`q_the_herd_stands_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "The herd will stand."*

> Good. I'll sleep in the barn till it's done. Don't tell Tamsin why.

**`q_the_herd_stands_offer__declined`** — *player says: "That's watch work, not mine."*

> The watch says the same. Somebody's wrong about whose work it is.

### Conversation: `q_the_herd_stands_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_herd_stands:ready)*

**`q_the_herd_stands_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Five. No red cloth since Tuesday, and the cows are eating like they know it. Here. A herd that stands is worth paying for.

## Keeper Ansel `keeper_ansel` — 18 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Lamp-oil and old paper. He walked the High Road three times end to end before his knees retired to the registry.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeper of the Waykeepers' Hall registry. Reverent, precise, a little dusty. Speaks in entries and dates; softens only at the memorial wall.

**Chatterbox casting:** `narrator/crypt_kirksvoice` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `keeper_ansel__bark_1` — "Every lamp on every road is a promise somebody keeps. I keep two of them and a book."
- `keeper_ansel__bark_2` — "The registry holds every name that walked north through our gate. Most came back. The hall's braziers burn for the rest."
- `keeper_ansel__bark_3` — "The Waykeepers were founded on the mountain, but the order lives wherever a lamp does."

### Conversation: `ansel_hall`

**`ansel_hall__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Peace on your road, traveler. The hall is open. It always is. Sit if you're footsore. I'm Ansel. I keep the lamps, the benches, and the book.

**`ansel_hall__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "faith"; or follows straight on from "book"*

> What would you know?

**`ansel_hall__faith`** — *player says: "What do the Waykeepers believe, exactly?"*

> Nothing you'd need a robe for. A lit lamp is a promise. Somebody keeps it, and somebody walks safer for it. We keep the lamps. That is the whole of the creed.

**`ansel_hall__book`** — *player says: "What's the book?"*

> The registry. Every soul who walks north through our gate signs it, or I sign for them. Most names take a homecoming mark within the year. Some never do. On feast nights I read the unmarked names to the braziers. Somebody should say them aloud once a season.

**`ansel_hall__order`** — *player says: "Tell me about the order."*

> Founded on the mountain, in the bad years after Silverfall sealed its deeps and the roads went feral. Marshal Kestrel's grandmother built the first waystation out of her own crew's wages. The Marshal keeps the order still, from the chapter house up there. Sergeants at the stations, Edda at the Last Lamp, and me at the southern end. I lit lamps on the High Road for eleven years, before the knees went.

**`ansel_hall__bye`** — *player says: "Peace on yours, Keeper."*

> Peace on your road. Sign the book before you walk north.

### Conversation: `ansel_registry` *(plays when: merra_edwin)*

**`ansel_registry__page`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've been to Merra's shop. People come from her wall to my book, and they always stand just where you're standing. Yes. Edwin's page is here. Signed north in his own hand, the spring of the early wolves. No homecoming mark.

**`ansel_registry__read`** — *follows straight on from "page"*

> I'll tell you what the registry knows that the cape on her wall doesn't: his caravan made the Fork. He gave his place at the palisade to a tinsmith's family and stood the last watch outside the wall himself. The sergeant's report says the lamps never went out that night. He kept them lit.

**`ansel_registry__knows`** — *player says: "Does Merra know?"*

> She knows the shape of it. She's never asked for the page, and I don't press. If she ever asks, the book is hers. Until then I read his name to the braziers each feast, and she keeps the cape clean. Between us he stays remembered. Thank you for asking.

**`ansel_registry__stand`** — *player says: "(Stand with him a moment.)"*

> Peace on his road, wherever it went. And on yours. Signed and marked, if I have any say in it.

### Conversation: `ansel_tollwar` *(plays when: dlg:ansel_hall)*

**`ansel_tollwar__notice`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've walked past the pillar by the bank. Everyone does, twice a day. Stone post, two braziers. I feed those braziers every evening at dusk. I'll tell you why, if you have the patience.

**`ansel_tollwar__chain`** — *player says: "Tell me about the Toll War."*

> Before your time, the Redmask brigands chained the ford. A chain, across the shallows this town is named for, and a toll to cross it. Coin at first. Then coin and goods. Then whatever they fancied, from whoever looked least able to argue.

**`ansel_tollwar__answer`** — *follows straight on from "chain"*

> The town answered. Farmers. The miller's boy. A sixteen-year-old gate runner named Aldis, who would not stay put. She keeps the north gate now. The chain came down and the ford ran free, and it cost us the names on that pillar. Cormund counted what the Redmasks had taken and built the bank so it could never be taken that way again.

**`ansel_tollwar__lamp`** — *follows straight on from "answer"*

> So: two braziers, fed at dusk, for as long as this hall stands. Go stand at the pillar some evening. You'll have company. The Captain comes at the end of her watch. She'd deny it, so don't ask her. Just stand quietly. The road stays free. The names on the stone paid for it.

### Conversation: `q_names_in_the_registry_offer` *(plays when: quest:names_in_the_registry:available)*

**`q_names_in_the_registry_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> An entry wants carrying. Silverfall keeps its own rolls, and old Skarn should hear this name spoken before he reads it. He was last man out of the deep galleries. Would you go up the mountain?

**`q_names_in_the_registry_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it. Where's Silverfall?"*

> Above the great falls, north and west. You'll hear the city before you see it. Skarn drinks where old soldiers drink. Ask for the man with the bad leg.

**`q_names_in_the_registry_offer__declined`** — *player says: "The mountain can wait."*

> Very well. The entry will keep.

### Conversation: `q_the_reavers_mark_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_reavers_mark:ready)*

**`q_the_reavers_mark_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> A reaver's mark, surrendered by force of arms. I'll enter it under today's date, with your name as witness. The Hall thanks you. I thank you. Both are now in the record.

*Sawdust on his cuffs, chalk on his fingers, a measuring string around his neck tied in a knot only he can undo.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Master artisan chasing one perfect chair before he dies. Soft-spoken, hands-first, apologizes for talking too long, then does. Gentle, thoughtful, slightly embarrassed by his own enthusiasm.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `master_tilo__bark_2` — "My sister Merra says I never finish anything. I'm three years into a chair that will prove her wrong."
- `master_tilo__bark_3` — "The hall's benches are for everyone. Bring your hands, I'll lend the patience."

### Conversation: `tilo_patterns`

**`tilo_patterns__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Oh, welcome, welcome. Mind the sawdust. Actually, no, don't. Sawdust on the floor means work on the bench. I'm Tilo. The loom, the carving bench, the worktable: all public, all yours. Sorry, I should let you speak.

**`tilo_patterns__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "public"; or follows straight on from "chair"*

> What can I do for you?

**`tilo_patterns__public`** — *player says: "Public? Anyone can use these stations?"*

**`tilo_patterns__chair`** — *player says: "Your sister says you never finish anything."*

> Merra told you about the chair. Of course she did. Three years, yes. Three years. But the chair is teaching me, you see. Every joint I cut for pay, I cut better, because the chair at home is watching. That sounded less strange in my head.

**`tilo_patterns__galleria`** — *player says: "You trained somewhere grand, I'd guess."*

> Silverfall's galleria. A clothier took me on as a boy to carry bolts up the Silver Stair. I came down before the deep trouble with one pattern-book and a needle case. Grand work up there. The useful work I learned here.

**`tilo_patterns__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the patterns."*

> Leather, cloth, and woodcraft patterns: the whole soft-trades ladder. Priced by what they'll ask of your hands.
