## Calder `fence_calder` — 12 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*A pleasant face you will struggle to describe afterward. His counter is spotless. His ledgers do not exist.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Fence, 'Purveyor of Provenance'. Euphemism as art form: everything 'found', 'orphaned', 'previously appreciated'. Silk-smooth, faintly delighted with his own vocabulary.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/gazlow_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `fence_calder__bark_1` — "Everything on this counter has a history. None of it is written down. That's the service."
- `fence_calder__bark_2` — "Runa stamps silver. I un-stamp it. The mountain provides for everyone."
- `fence_calder__bark_3` — "You didn't find this place. The alley let you in. There's a difference, and Pike keeps track of it."

### Conversation: `calder_counter`

**`calder_counter__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome, welcome. No names needed. I find they clutter a sale. Everything on this counter has a history and none of it is written down. That's the service.

**`calder_counter__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "goods"; or follows straight on from "watch"*

> Buying, selling, or practicing your questions? The first two are quicker.

**`calder_counter__goods`** — *player says: "Where do your goods come from?"*

> From around. Caravans lighten themselves on the High Road, the Undercroft coughs up curiosities, estates get settled faster than the heirs expected. I ask no questions coming in, so I can honestly answer none going out. If provenance matters to you, Vigdis is up the walk, and she charges for all that paper.

**`calder_counter__watch`** — *player says: "Aren't you worried about the watch?"*

> The watch doesn't come past the scree, per an arrangement above both our stations. And understand: Mab has rules stricter than any magistrate. Nothing from city homes, nothing from the shrine, nothing that got anyone hurt on this mountain. Break those and you don't answer to the watch. You answer to her.

**`calder_counter__browse`** — *player says: "Let's see the counter."*

> The counter, then. Keys of uncertain doors, leather of flexible biography, and sundries. Coin only. Smile optional.

**`calder_counter__bye`** — *player says: "No questions asked, Calder."*

> A pleasure doing nothing memorable with you.

### Conversation: `q_the_gilded_cage_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_gilded_cage:available)*

**`q_the_gilded_cage_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> A commission, since you're now a colleague. A locket, gold over brass, sentimental weight considerable, was orphaned some years ago when a courier misjudged the first climb. It remains with the, ah, current residents of the watchtower there.

**`q_the_gilded_cage_offer__residents`** — *player says: "Current residents?"*

> The tower's old garrison. Previously alive. They observe traditional hours: sunset onward. By day you'll find swept stone and a view. Go at night, and go armed.

**`q_the_gilded_cage_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll recover it."; or player says: "Night it is."*

> The shielded ones keep the good things. The watch always did. Bring the locket whole and unopened. Provenance is my trade.

**`q_the_gilded_cage_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find another colleague."*

> Pity. It was a very reasonable commission, considering the residents.

### Conversation: `q_the_gilded_cage_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_gilded_cage:ready)*

**`q_the_gilded_cage_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> gilded locket Whole, unopened. You'd be surprised how few manage the second part.

**`q_the_gilded_cage_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> The clasp still works. Somewhere there's a family that stopped waiting for this. One of my quieter errands will see it home. That part isn't business. The ring is, though: payment, previously appreciated, now yours.

## Fletcher Haki `fletcher_haki` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*A quiet man with feather-callused thumbs. Ten years a Waykeeper before the road gave him back.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Fletcher; Waykeeper veteran invalided off the road with a bad knee. Careful, oath-driven: every arrow is somebody's life. Understates his ten years on the road. Quiet pride, no bitterness aloud.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/george` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `fletcher_haki__bark_1` — "Ten years walking the High Road for Kestrel's order. Now I make the arrows and other people do the walking. Fair trade."
- `fletcher_haki__bark_2` — "Straight grain, true flight. The saw yard keeps its best billets for me and the wolves down-mountain wish it didn't."
- `fletcher_haki__bark_3` — "The watch shoots what I fletch. I fletch like their lives depend on it, because I remember when mine did."

### Conversation: `haki_flight`

**`haki_flight__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> One moment. A fletch set wrong kills someone eight weeks from now, far from here. There. Done. Now you have my whole attention.

**`haki_flight__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "road"; or follows straight on from "watch"*

> Ask, friend.

**`haki_flight__road`** — *player says: "You were a Waykeeper?"*

> Ten years under Kestrel's banner, walking the High Road with a lamp and a bow. The road gave me back with a knee that predicts weather, and one rule: never send anyone into the dark with gear you wouldn't stake your own life on. I can't walk the miles anymore. So I fletch.

**`haki_flight__watch`** — *player says: "Who do you fletch for?"*

> The watch on the wall. The castle guard. Kestrel's sergeants. Any honest traveler with coin and sense. When a watchman on the night wall nocks one of mine, he's holding my word that it flies true.

**`haki_flight__true`** — *player says: "What makes an arrow true?"*

> Straight grain. The saw yard saves me its best billets. Feathers matched from the same wing, or the arrow corkscrews. And patience at the finish. That's the whole craft.

**`haki_flight__bye`** — *player says: "Fly straight, Fletcher."*

> Fly straight. And thank the goose.

## Foreman Grettir `foreman_grettir` — 20 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Stone dust in every seam of him. He counts his crews out and counts them back, and the counting is the whole of his religion.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Yard foreman; his brother's crew was the count that never came back from the Undercroft. NEAR-SILENT. Two-line answers. Approaches the brother only sideways, and the '...' in his lines is him stepping around it. Low, guarded, closed.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/veil_ethan` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.6 · cfg 0.603

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `foreman_grettir__bark_1` — "Helmets on past the rope line. Yes, you."
- `foreman_grettir__bark_2` — "The upper vein? We don't discuss the upper vein. It and I have an arrangement and you're not in it."
- `foreman_grettir__bark_3` — "Every crew goes down on my count and comes up on my count. Twenty years, the numbers have matched. There was a time before that. We don't discuss that either."

### Conversation: `grettir_yard`

**`grettir_yard__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Helmets past the rope line. Grettir. Foreman. Here to swing a pick, the mountain pays honest wages. Here to ask about the upper vein, we're done early.

**`grettir_yard__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "vein"; or follows straight on from "mining"*

> What?

**`grettir_yard__vein`** — *player says: "What's the upper vein?"*

> The one we don't discuss. Mithril. You'd hear it from some coal boy anyway. Runs shallow at the top of the deep galleries. Every foreman before me left it alone. I leave it alone. The reasons are between me and the mountain. Dig anywhere else in my yard with my blessing.

**`grettir_yard__mining`** — *player says: "How goes the mining?"*

> Silver holds. Iron's steady. Coal does what coal does. My crews go down on my count and come up on my count. Twenty years, every count matched. Now the deep's open again, half my shift wants transfer papers. Better ore down there. Worse neighbors. I sign the papers. I count them extra.

**`grettir_yard__below`** — *player says: "I've been below. The old galleries are worked again."*

> You've talked to Coppin, then. So you've stood in the old works. My brother's crew cut those galleries, before the trouble. He was setting shot-holes past the rubble line the day the kobolds came through, and the seal went up with the count unmatched. First unmatched count in the yard's books. If the reeve's crews ever clear the far warren, there'll be tools down there with our mark on the hafts. I'd want to know. That's all. I'd want to know.

**`grettir_yard__word`** — *player says: "If I find anything with your mark, I'll bring word."*

> Aye. Well. The yard's grateful, and the yard doesn't say that often. Helmets past the rope line, traveler. Even below. Especially below.

**`grettir_yard__sorry`** — *player says: "I'm sorry, Foreman."*

> Twenty years of practice at it. Go on now. The count doesn't keep itself.

**`grettir_yard__bye`** — *player says: "I'll leave you to your count."*

> Count yourself out at the rope. Everyone counts out. House rule.

**`grettir_yard__named`** — *player says: "The names are cut. Petra set them where the seal stood."*

> I know. I went up at night to read them. Fourteen names, good stone. Back to work.

### Conversation: `q_the_brothers_tools_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_brothers_tools:available)*

**`q_the_brothers_tools_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You know about my brother. So. The kobolds carry the crew's tools. Guild mark on every head. I want three back.

**`q_the_brothers_tools_offer__where`** — *player says: "Where do I look?"*

> Past the Deep Market. The choked tunnel, southeast. Warrens are through the gap.

**`q_the_brothers_tools_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll bring them back."; or player says: "I'll go."*

> Three. Enough that it isn't luck.

**`q_the_brothers_tools_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not now."*

> Twenty years. It keeps.

### Conversation: `q_the_brothers_tools_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_brothers_tools:ready)*

**`q_the_brothers_tools_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Give them here.

**`q_the_brothers_tools_turnin__held`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> ...That's his strike on this one. Shallow on the upstroke. He never fixed that.

**`q_the_brothers_tools_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "held"*

> The yard owes you wages. Take them. And thank you. Subject's closed.

### Conversation: `q_thin_the_warrens_offer` *(plays when: quest:thin_the_warrens:available)*

**`q_thin_the_warrens_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Kobolds. Warrens off the mountain works. Eight.

**`q_thin_the_warrens_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Why eight?"*

> Eight's what creeps back in a span. Count right.

**`q_thin_the_warrens_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Send the yard."*

> Yard doesn't go there. That's the point.

### Conversation: `q_thin_the_warrens_turnin` *(plays when: quest:thin_the_warrens:ready)*

**`q_thin_the_warrens_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Eight. Good count. Wage is there. Same work next span. They creep back. They always have.

## Forgemistress Balla `forgemistress_balla` — 11 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Shoulders that have argued with mithril and won. The forge quiets a little when she crosses it, out of respect.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Forgemistress; wants steel with no lies in it. LOUD, certain, generous with praise for work, never for people directly. The thirty-year feud with Koll is theatre both maintain. Big voice, big room.

**Chatterbox casting:** `news/iron_sue` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.778 · cfg 0.534

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `forgemistress_balla__bark_1` — "You're standing in the Grand Forge. Stand straighter."
- `forgemistress_balla__bark_2` — "Bretta Ironhewn keeps a forge at the ford now. Best rival I ever had. Tell her the anvil's still here. She'll know which one."
- `forgemistress_balla__bark_3` — "Silver is vanity. Steel is honest work. Starfall is a rumor I mean to hammer myself."

### Conversation: `balla_forge`

**`balla_forge__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You're in the Grand Forge of Silverfall. Stand straighter. Good. Now then: steel, silver, or conversation?

**`balla_forge__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "trials"; or follows straight on from "bretta"*

> Well?

**`balla_forge__trials`** — *player says: "Tell me about the anvil trials."*

> Every apprentice generation, one anvil, two finalists, best blade takes the forge-right. My year it was me and Bretta Ironhewn, and the judges took until dawn. I won on the temper line. She'd tell you she won on everything else. She'd be half right.

**`balla_forge__bretta`** — *player says: "Bretta Ironhewn says your quenches ran cold."*

> HA! Twenty years and she's still filing that grievance! My quenches ran precise. She calls that cold. You've seen her, then. The ford forge. Good. Tell her the anvil's still here, the solstice letter stands, and the door's never been locked. Tell her that last part like it's from the forge, not from me.

**`balla_forge__work`** — *player says: "What's the forge working on?"*

> Silver for the bank, steel for the watch, and now the deep orders. The reopened galleries want rails, brackets, cage-lanterns, pick heads by the crate. Biggest commission this forge has taken since the terraces went up. Listen. Hear that? Three anvils going at once. My smiths are singing again. THAT'S good work.

**`balla_forge__browse`** — *player says: "Show me your stock."*

> Bar stock and coal, priced by the ledger, weighed in front of you. The Grand Forge doesn't haggle. The price is already fair.

### Conversation: `q_steel_for_the_stair_offer` *(plays when: quest:steel_for_the_stair:available)*

**`q_steel_for_the_stair_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You there. Hands. The stair rails are going to steel this season and my stock won't cover it. Six iron bars, eight of coal, on this bench, weighed. That's the whole commission.

**`q_steel_for_the_stair_offer__where`** — *player says: "Smelted where?"*

> Anywhere honest! Smelt it yourself at Koll's furnaces if your arms are up to it, or buy off Varga's scales in the Deep Market. Half my stock walks up that stair anyway. I pay by weight.

**`q_steel_for_the_stair_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "You'll have it."; or player says: "Weight it is."*

> Good. When I strike this steel it will NOT lie to me. See your iron doesn't either. There's a pattern in it for you. Buckler work. My best teaching piece.

**`q_steel_for_the_stair_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find other hands."*

> Then stand clear of the sparks. The rails won't wait forever and neither do I.

### Conversation: `q_steel_for_the_stair_turnin` *(plays when: quest:steel_for_the_stair:ready)*

**`q_steel_for_the_stair_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> On the bench. Weighed, and it's ALL true weight. No slag, no lies. THIS is stock! The rails will outlive the stair, and the work was good. Take the buckler pattern and the coin. Now clear the bench, I have steel to make.

## Ivo `gardener_ivo` — 4 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Sunburnt at altitude, soil to the wrists. Talks to the wheat rows in a tone most people save for children and dogs.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Gardener of the Greenstair; talks to plants more easily than people. Quiet, halting with strangers, suddenly fluent about green things. Let the fluency switch on when the subject turns to growing.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/belf_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.551

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `gardener_ivo__bark_1` — "Oh. Hello. Mind the rows, they mind back."
- `gardener_ivo__bark_2` — "Cold ground makes a sweet carrot. Nobody believes me until they taste one."
- `gardener_ivo__bark_3` — "Snow in the morning, sun by noon, wind all day. You plant for the row, not the field."

### Conversation: `ivo_greenstair`

**`ivo_greenstair__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "how"; or follows straight on from "grow"*

> Oh. A visitor. Hello. Um. This is the Greenstair. Highest farm in the Dawnlands. That's the interesting fact about it. Did you need something?

**`ivo_greenstair__how`** — *player says: "How do you farm a mountain?"*

> Terraces, and patience. Snow in the morning, sun by noon, wind all day. You plant for the row, not the field. Each row has its own weather up here. Its own temper, really. That one by the fence sulks if the wheat crowds it. People think I'm joking when I say that. I'm not.

**`ivo_greenstair__grow`** — *player says: "What do you grow up here?"*

> Wheat and cotton on the high pads. Sagewort and moonbell behind the fence. Those are for Wyn, the herbalist. She's particular and so are they, so it works. And carrots. Cold ground makes a carrot sweet. Most of them go to Signy, the cook, for her stew. The carrots don't mind. They like Signy.

**`ivo_greenstair__bye`** — *player says: "Keep at it, Ivo."*

> Mind the rows. And take a carrot, if one's leaning. The leaning ones have decided.

## Herald Ossian `herald_ossian` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Reads the Line's decrees in a voice that fills the hall, then spends the rest of the day saving his own. The tabard is madder crimson and immaculate.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Reads the Line's decrees in a voice that fills the hall, then spends the rest of the day saving it. Two registers: the declamation, and the smaller private one he actually talks in. Play the small one unless the line is a proclamation.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/murozond_m` *(provisional)* · exaggeration undefined · cfg undefined

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `herald_ossian__bark_1` — "Hall at morning bell, Grand Court at midday. The word walks down the stair so the city need not walk up."
- `herald_ossian__bark_2` — "I read what the Crown writes. What I think is kept in a smaller voice, for after supper."
- `herald_ossian__bark_3` — "Hear the word and mind the edge. That second part is mine. The Crown lets me keep it."

### Conversation: `ossian_word`

**`ossian_word__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> If you heard a big voice on the stair at midday, that was me, but this is the small one. The big voice belongs to the Crown. This one is off duty.

**`ossian_word__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "decree"; or follows straight on from "walk"*

> Quickly, then. The bell owns me at the hour.

**`ossian_word__decree`** — *player says: "What did the Crown decree today?"*

> Tithe day moved for the smelter's relining. Two names raised to the watch. A caution on the Hoargate road, which is the same caution as always, which is the pass. The Crown's decrees are mostly weather, traveler. That is what good rule sounds like. Dull, on schedule, signed.

**`ossian_word__walk`** — *player says: "Why walk the word down the stair yourself?"*

> Because the city should not have to climb for its own news. Hall at morning bell for the household, Grand Court at midday for everyone else. The King's grandfather had it cried at the castle gate only, and wondered why the Row heard everything a day late and backwards.

**`ossian_word__words`** — *player says: "Do you ever change the words?"*

> Never the words. Once, the order. I read the watch promotions before the tithe change, because Old Brandt's daughter was in the square and her name deserved the crowd. The Queen noticed. The Queen notices everything. She said the sums were unharmed and let it stand.

**`ossian_word__bye`** — *player says: "Keep your small voice, Herald."*

> Hear the word and mind the edge. The second part is mine.

## Wyn `herbalist_wyn` — 5 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Smells of crushed sagewort and clean snow. Speaks softly, as though the tinctures were sleeping.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Herbalist; wants people to stop being stupid about mushrooms. Brisk, clinical, unexpectedly funny about symptoms. The humor is dry and entirely accidental-sounding.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/spite_vex` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `herbalist_wyn__bark_1` — "The ledge-flowers up here bloom a week later and last a month longer. Everything at altitude learns to hold on."
- `herbalist_wyn__bark_2` — "I send a crate of tinctures down to Edda's lamp every season. She sends back complaints and empty bottles, which from Edda is warm correspondence."
- `herbalist_wyn__bark_3` — "Drink the green one for wounds, the amber for weariness, and water for most things people buy potions for."

### Conversation: `wyn_remedies`

**`wyn_remedies__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Come in quietly, if you would. The tinctures settle better in a calm room. I'm Wyn. Wounds, weariness, and everything the mountain does to lowland lungs: somewhere on these shelves is the answer.

**`wyn_remedies__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "flora"; or follows straight on from "edda"*

> What do you need?

**`wyn_remedies__flora`** — *player says: "What grows this high?"*

> More than the lowlands credit. Ledge-flowers that bloom late and hold long. Sagewort gone small and fierce with the altitude. Half the dose does twice the work, mind that if you buy it. And snow-moss the rams won't touch, which is how you know it's medicine.

**`wyn_remedies__edda`** — *player says: "You trade with the Last Lamp?"*

> A crate of tinctures down to Edda's lamp every season, since before the trade had my name on it. She sends back the empties and a note that says the same thing every year: 'still alive, no thanks needed, the amber one wants more bite.' From Edda, that counts as fondness. Her sister keeps our shrine. The stubbornness runs in the family.

**`wyn_remedies__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the remedies."*

> Green for wounds, amber for weariness, and the salve for everything the road rubs raw.

## Osa `hostler_osa` — 7 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Sixty-some years, most of them opinions. Mules trust her on sight.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Hostler; Dunna's mam, wants word from the ford more than she'll admit. Horse-first, people-second; gruff; melts at Dunna's name and pretends she didn't. Rough warmth badly hidden.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/flint_greta` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.667 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `hostler_osa__bark_1` — "Beasts watered, wheels mended, advice free."
- `hostler_osa__bark_2` — "I kept an inn at the ford for thirty years. My daughter keeps it now, Dunna, at the Wanderer's Rest. Her stew wants thyme."
- `hostler_osa__bark_3` — "Walked the High Road at sixty, alone. Everyone said it would kill me. It didn't."

### Conversation: `osa_yard`

**`osa_yard__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the trough. The mules queue politer than the caravans do. Osa. Hostler. You've the road on your boots; sit on a rail and scrape it off while you talk.

**`osa_yard__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "climb"; or follows straight on from "dunna"*

> Go on then.

**`osa_yard__climb`** — *player says: "You came up the High Road at sixty?"*

> Sixty years old, one pack, uphill, alone, the spring after my man died. The whole ford said the road would kill me. It didn't.

**`osa_yard__dunna`** — *player says: "I know your daughter. Dunna, at the ford."*

> You've sat at my daughter's bar. Well? Did the stew want thyme? It wanted thyme. It ALWAYS wants thyme. Thirty years I ran that room, and she won't take one herb of advice from me. Which is exactly what I was like. So, fair play. You see her again, tell her the mountain air is kind, her mother's hips are winning, and the thyme grows wild ten steps from her own back door. She'll ignore all three. Tell her anyway.

**`osa_yard__yard`** — *player says: "What passes through this yard?"*

> Everything the mountain buys and everything it sells, with mules in between. Silver down, cotton up, deep-ore out of the new cellar, and every kind of traveler the road makes. They go up to the Undercroft eager and come back quiet. The mules prefer them quiet.

**`osa_yard__stable`** — *player says: "Any of the coursers for sale?"*

> The coursers, aye. Not the mules. Bay, grey, and the dun. Sound feet, road manners, shod for the long miles. Coin buys the saddle and the beast wears it. Look them over.

**`osa_yard__bye`** — *player says: "Rest easy, Osa."*

> Walk well. And eat something before the Silver Stair. It's a long climb on an empty stomach.

## Innkeep Ragna `innkeep_ragna` — 7 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*A bar rag over one shoulder and the whole city's news behind her eyes. Nothing said in the Flagon stays in the Flagon unless she decides it does.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Keeper of the Silver Flagon; wants a quieter room than Dunna's and pretends not to compete. Composed, discreet, hears everything, repeats little. Smooth, level, professionally pleasant.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/hush_morrow` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `innkeep_ragna__bark_1` — "Beds, board, and the news first. The news is free. The beds are not, and don't let anyone tell you the board is."
- `innkeep_ragna__bark_2` — "Signy lodges in my guest wing and cooks in her own kitchen, and the day those two facts trade places this city falls apart."
- `innkeep_ragna__bark_3` — "Dunna keeps the inn at the ford; I keep the one at the top. What we know between us never goes in writing."

### Conversation: `ragna_flagon`

**`ragna_flagon__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome to the Silver Flagon. Beds, board, and quiet. We keep all three. Wipe your boots, if you would.

**`ragna_flagon__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "news"; or player says: "Back to the bar."*

> What can the house do for you?

**`ragna_flagon__news`** — *player says: "What's the news, then?"*

> What I can repeat: Lantern Row has the price of arcane dust up again. The Deep Market talk says the kobolds are digging toward something. And the Queen walked the mere at noon and fed the shrine fire with her own hand. The rest is my lodgers' business.

**`ragna_flagon__lodgers`** — *player says: "Who lodges here?"*

> Signy the terrace cook keeps my best room and pays half in leftovers, which suits us both. Caravan masters. Guildhall clerks in audit season. A Waykeeper now and then, too stiff for the chapter house cots. And sometimes a guest takes the corner room, pays in advance, and asks nothing. I ask nothing back.

**`ragna_flagon__dunna`** — *player says: "You know Dunna at the ford?"*

> Dunna keeps the inn at the bottom of the road. I keep the one at the top. We trade the road's news through the caravans, twice a season, and never once in writing. Her mother Osa waters the mules at our own gate. The day those two are in one room again, pull up a chair. Quietly.

**`ragna_flagon__browse`** — *player says: "What's on the board?"*

> Stew with real beef in it, bread from Signy's ovens, and a short board. A short board means nothing on it is old. Sit where you like.

**`ragna_flagon__bye`** — *player says: "Warm hearths, Innkeep."*

> Warm hearths. The door's never barred before midnight.

## King Aeriex `king_aeriex` — 18 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Winter-pale as the high snow, still as the mere. The crown sits on him heavily, and looks as though it always has.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Fifth king of the Silver Line, a quarry foreman's grandson who knows it. PLAIN. Shorter and simpler than visitors expect from a king; that plainness is the character. No royal ornament, no boom. A working man's gravity.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/male/veil_ethan` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `king_aeriex__bark_1` — "My grandfather cut the third terrace. My father paved the road you climbed. I sign papers."
- `king_aeriex__bark_2` — "The moonpale runs in the Line. My grandmother said the mountain keeps our color so we can never deny the kinship."
- `king_aeriex__bark_3` — "Ask the Queen anything I just told you. If our answers differ, hers is the true one."

### Conversation: `aeriex_court`

**`aeriex_court__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> The guards let you through, which means you climbed the High Road on your own feet. Come in, then.

**`aeriex_court__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "line"; or player says: "Something else, Majesty."*

> Ask. I'm told kings are supposed to make people wait. My grandfather was a quarry foreman. Waiting wastes daylight.

**`aeriex_court__line`** — *player says: "What is the Silver Line?"*

> Five kings, one name. The first Aeriex was a quarry foreman who paid the shepherds' debts in silver. Folk called him king for it, half as a joke, and the name held. The bargain hasn't changed since: the Crown pays first, and the roads stay lit.

**`aeriex_court__maren`** — *player says: "Who really runs this mountain?"*

> Maren speaks for the mountain. She was Castellan under my father; she'll be Castellan under my heir, if she consents to it. When she says a gallery is unsafe, it closes before I've finished nodding.

**`aeriex_court__rookery`** — *player says: "You know about the Rookery, don't you."*

> Yes. Behind the bank, past the scree. The Magpie's people were quarrymen before my family were kings; if we're honest about it, theirs is the older claim. They watch what my watch can't. I leave them their dark, and it stays civil.

**`aeriex_court__seal`** — *player says: "Why open the Undercroft after twenty years?"*

> Twenty years my father kept his grief sealed behind good stonework, and the kobolds dug on regardless. Maren came to me with the surveys and said the seal was keeping out miners and nothing else. I gave the order the same hour. If we must fight for the deep, I'd rather do it with the lamps lit.

**`aeriex_court__bye`** — *player says: "Long reign to you, Majesty."*

> And a good road to you. Mind the edge.

### Conversation: `q_the_kings_peace_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_kings_peace:available)*

**`q_the_kings_peace_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You came recommended by the registry, which is the only recommendation I read. Here's the work: brigands are camped on the open road again. My grandfather's grandfather saw the ford chained once. We don't do that twice.

**`q_the_kings_peace_offer__why`** — *player says: "Why me and not the watch?"*

> The watch holds walls. Roads need someone who walks them anyway. That's you, or I've read the registry wrong.

**`q_the_kings_peace_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll break the camps."; or player says: "You read it right."*

> Camps first, archers included. Then whoever keeps their shares. There's always one. The Crown pays when the road is quiet, not before.

**`q_the_kings_peace_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'm not ready for crown work."; or player says: "Maybe later."*

> Honest answer. Come back when you are.

### Conversation: `q_the_kings_peace_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_kings_peace:ready)*

**`q_the_kings_peace_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> The road reports quiet and the reaver's name is off the books. Good work, plainly done. My grandfather's grandfather paid the shepherds' debts with quarry wages. I pay road-work with the treasury. Same bargain.

### Conversation: `q_the_silver_line_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_silver_line:available)*

**`q_the_silver_line_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've done the queen's errand and walked the Marshal's line. One more, and it's the heaviest. The high passes are turning bold: trolls off the scree, worgs on the shepherds' shoulders. The Line holds because someone does the work. This season, I'm asking you.

**`q_the_silver_line_offer__after`** — *player says: "What comes after?"*

> After, you present yourself to the Castellan. Maren weighs who the Crown may trust, and she doesn't take my word for it. That's why her word is worth having.

**`q_the_silver_line_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll clear the passes."; or player says: "Then I'll earn hers too."*

> Two trolls, four worgs, and the shepherds sleep again. Then the Castellan. Then me. Go steady.

**`q_the_silver_line_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Not yet."*

> The mountain keeps. So does the offer.

### Conversation: `q_the_silver_line_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_silver_line:ready)*

**`q_the_silver_line_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> The Castellan sent one line: 'Sound.' From Maren, that's high praise.

**`q_the_silver_line_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> The passes are clear and the Line owes you. So it pays: plate from the wardens' own pattern, struck in my armory. My grandfather's grandfather was a quarry foreman who paid other people's debts. Wear it, and you'll be keeping his books.

## Pike `lookout_pike` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Perched on a crate with a whittling knife and a view of everything. The whittling never seems to produce anything. The view does.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Rookery lookout; sees everything, says nothing. Minimal, sardonic, roof-slang; rarely finishes a warning, expects you to catch up. Half the line is in the shrug.

- `lookout_pike__bark_3` — "The Undercroft stair's behind the arch. Mab's people keep the braziers fed. We use it more than the miners ever did."

**`q_the_bear_of_the_spine_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You. Den-breaker. Word climbs faster than people. Bears on the near shoulders. Trolls behind. Two and two, before the snow.

**`q_the_bear_of_the_spine_offer__who`** — *player says: "Who's asking, you or the city?"*

**`q_the_bear_of_the_spine_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

## The Magpie `magpie_mab` — 25 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Small, still, and dressed like dusk. You notice her rings first, then that she has already finished noticing you.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** The Magpie, mistress of the Rookery; the city's shadows kept orderly. Never answers a question first; asks one back. Soft, unhurried, everything a trade. Quiet enough that people lean in; that's the point.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/hush_morrow` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `magpie_mab__bark_1` — "The Rookery was here before the castle. Quarrymen's tents, then quarrymen's shacks, then quarrymen's grandchildren who found quieter work."
- `magpie_mab__bark_2` — "The Crown tolerates us because I let it see enough. The watch holds the wall. Somebody has to hold everything the wall can't see."
- `magpie_mab__bark_3` — "No lamps back here. A lamp tells the dark where you are, and the dark writes it down."

### Conversation: `mab_fine` *(plays when: faction:rookery:atmost:outlaw)*

**`mab_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> You want something washed. Tell me: what do you think a clean name costs, in a house that keeps its floors swept?

**`mab_fine__quote`** — *player says: "You tell me."*

> A fair question. It deserves arithmetic.

**`mab_fine__pay`** — *player says: "Whatever it is, I'll pay."*

> Everything here is a trade. This one is even simple.

**`mab_fine__bye`** — *player says: "Forget it."*

> Already forgotten. That costs nothing. Once.

### Conversation: `mab_rookery`

**`mab_rookery__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Sit if you like. Pike gave you one whistle, so you get to talk to me. I'm Mab. The city calls me the Magpie. It thinks that stings. Now, what carried you up my ledge?

**`mab_rookery__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "rookery"; or player says: "Something else."*

> Ask what you came to ask. Curiosity is the only coin we don't take here. We just note who spends it.

**`mab_rookery__rookery`** — *player says: "What is this place?"*

> Older than the castle, and I can prove it in stone. The first quarrymen pitched camp here, out of the wind, over the workings. Then an Aeriex got called king, the terraces got grand, and somebody drew the city's maps around us. Do we mind? A quarter the maps forget suits us well. We're the quarrymen's grandchildren. We found quieter work. Mostly.

**`mab_rookery__crown`** — *player says: "The Crown just allows you?"*

> Tolerates is the castle's word. Mine is arrangement. The watch holds the wall and the road, but a city's real trouble comes up its alleys, and the alleys are ours. When something moves in the dark that shouldn't, the castle hears of it before its own spies do. In exchange: no lamps back here, no ledgers, no questions at Calder's counter. Aeriex's father shook on it. Aeriex keeps it.

**`mab_rookery__stair`** — *player says: "Why keep the Undercroft braziers fed?"*

> Because we use it more than the miners ever did. The Undercroft's back ways were our roads for twenty sealed years. You can move a great deal through a mountain everyone believes is shut. Now the seal's broken and the Deep Market pays rent to the Crown, and my people still keep those braziers fed. Habits outlive their reasons.

**`mab_rookery__swept`** — *player says: "Coppin said the Deep Market floor was found swept."*

> So Coppin talks. Twenty years that floor stayed swept, and the city calls it a mystery, as if the mountain did its own housekeeping. It was my people. Down the back ways, once a season, with brooms and lamp-oil. My grandmother said you keep a road open by keeping it swept, and the Undercroft was always going to be needed again. Tell whoever you like. Nobody official will believe the rogues kept faith with the deep.

**`mab_rookery__bye`** — *player says: "Shadows keep you, Mab."*

> Shadows keep you. Leave by the ledge and Pike will think better of you.

**`mab_rookery__plumbing`** — *player says: "I've carried the pocket-word myself. The floor stays swept."*

> So you have. Do you know what that makes you? No, truly, I'm asking. Even I don't have a word for the ones who carry it and come back. Colleague will do until something quieter turns up.

### Conversation: `q_a_quiet_word_offer` *(plays when: quest:a_quiet_word:available)*

**`q_a_quiet_word_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You kept the floor's secret. So, a question for you: do you know what a person who keeps secrets is worth in this city?

**`q_a_quiet_word_offer__worth`** — *player says: "Tell me."; or player says: "Depends who's buying."*

> Neither do I, until I've seen their hands. Calder keeps a counter at the Broken Lantern, behind the scree. Go and be looked at. He'll have a small ask. Small asks are how I count.

**`q_a_quiet_word_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll pay the visit."*

> Mind the alley by the bank wall. Or don't. Finding the other way in would also tell me something.

**`q_a_quiet_word_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I don't deal in shadows."*

> No? Then who did I just watch keep one?

### Conversation: `q_a_quiet_word_turnin` *(plays when: quest:a_quiet_word:ready)*

**`q_a_quiet_word_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Two keys, and Calder says you're promisingly unremarkable. High praise. Keep it that way. The Rookery knows your face now. Your coin's on the table.

### Conversation: `q_the_arrangement_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_arrangement:available)*

**`q_the_arrangement_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've stood in the court. Tell me. Did anyone up there mention how a city this clean keeps its shadows so tidy?

**`q_the_arrangement_offer__arrangement`** — *player says: "There's an arrangement."; or player says: "No one mentioned shadows."*

> There's an understanding, and understandings need tending, by someone both sides can pretend they didn't send. Two calls. Bursar Odele, at the bank: ask if the tithe balances. Marshal Kestrel, at the chapter house: tell her the sweeping is done and the floor is clean.

**`q_the_arrangement_offer__know`** — *player says: "And they'll just know?"*

> Odele will say the arithmetic is unquestionable. Kestrel will make a face. Both of those are answers. You'll bring me the second one.

**`q_the_arrangement_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll make the calls."; or player says: "Done."*

> Softly, colleague. Keep this one in your pocket.

**`q_the_arrangement_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'd rather not know."*

> Wise, possibly. The floor stays swept either way.

### Conversation: `q_the_arrangement_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_arrangement:ready)*

**`q_the_arrangement_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Well? The face.

**`q_the_arrangement_turnin__face`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> 'Like she'd bitten a coin and found it real.' Yes. That's the one she makes. Twenty years of that face, and the roads still think the Rookery is a rumor.

**`q_the_arrangement_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "face"*

> The arrangement holds, then, and you're part of the sweeping now. The seeker stone is yours. It finds things. So do you.

## Marshal Kestrel `marshal_kestrel` — 29 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*The road made flesh: weathered, direct, and carrying the whole map of the High Road behind her eyes.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Marshal of the Waykeepers, holding the roads with too few people. Muster-roll clip, tired, dry. Quotes her grandmother once, reluctantly. The exhaustion is real but never asks for sympathy.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/flint_greta` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.644 · cfg 0.586

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `marshal_kestrel__bark_1` — "Every lamp between here and the ford answers to this room. Sit down if you've news; stand if you've complaints."
- `marshal_kestrel__bark_2` — "My grandmother built the first waystation out of her own crew's wages and a temper. The order keeps both traditions."
- `marshal_kestrel__bark_3` — "Edda taught me the lamp drill when I was nine. She'll outlast the mountain out of pure disapproval of the alternative."

### Conversation: `kestrel_chapter`

**`kestrel_chapter__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Chapter house of the Waykeepers. If you walked the High Road to get here, you've already met my order: the lamps, the palisades, the sergeants who checked the road behind you. Sit. Travelers' news is welcome in this room.

**`kestrel_chapter__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "founding"; or player says: "Something else."*

> What's your business with the order?

**`kestrel_chapter__founding`** — *player says: "How did the Waykeepers begin?"*

> My grandmother was a caravan mistress in the bad years after the seal. Roads feral, lamps dark, every ford tolled at knife-point. She built the first waystation at her own crew's expense and posted one rule over the door: the lamp stays lit. The order is that rule, with better funding. Forty years, three stations, one Last Lamp, and a registry of everyone the road has kept.

**`kestrel_chapter__sergeants`** — *player says: "Who keeps the road, day to day?"*

> Sergeants Hale, Odessa, and Brant hold the stations by rotation. Edda holds the Last Lamp and won't be relieved. Keeper Ansel holds the ford end and the registry. Add every crofter who feeds a traveler and every watch that walks a wall. Auxiliaries, sworn or not. Me, I move too few people along too much road, and I do the paperwork.

**`kestrel_chapter__hask`** — *player says: "I met an old Waykeeper at the ford. Hask."*

> Sergeant Hask. Fifteen years, the middle marches, and the worg winter that cost him two of his own inside the Fork's fence. He hung up the cloak and took up outfitting, and I'll tell you what I told the moot: the man still serves.

**`kestrel_chapter__bye`** — *player says: "Keep the lamps lit, Marshal."*

> Road keep you. And if you pass a dark lamp anywhere on my road, tell someone.

**`kestrel_chapter__walked`** — *player says: "I took all four reports myself, remember."*

> I remember. The muster-book has a mark by your name now: 'walked the line, full length'. There are sergeants without that mark. Don't tell them I said so.

### Conversation: `kestrel_fine` *(plays when: faction:waykeepers:atmost:outlaw)*

**`kestrel_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> You're on my roll with a mark against you. Coin clears it.

**`kestrel_fine__quote`** — *player says: "How much?"*

> He checks the roll.

**`kestrel_fine__pay`** — *player says: "Clear it."*

> He takes the count without looking up.

**`kestrel_fine__bye`** — *player says: "Leave the mark."*

> Suit yourself. The lamps see fine either way.

### Conversation: `q_short_handed_offer` *(plays when: quest:short_handed:available)*

**`q_short_handed_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Roll's short. Wolves between the lamps again. Six put down is a shift I don't have a warden for. You're not my first choice. You're the one standing here.

**`q_short_handed_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll walk the shift."*

> Lamp to lamp. Don't be clever about it.

**`q_short_handed_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find another."*

> There isn't another. That was the point.

### Conversation: `q_short_handed_turnin` *(plays when: quest:short_handed:ready)*

**`q_short_handed_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six. Noted on the roll, next to your mark. Take your pay.

### Conversation: `q_the_lamps_of_the_line_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_lamps_of_the_line:available)*

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> Muster stands at too few, same as last season. I need the whole line walked: every sergeant's report, taken in person, bottom of the road to the top. You've done crown work. This is the older kind.

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_offer__why`** — *player says: "Why in person?"*

> Because paper says 'quiet' and a sergeant's face says which kind of quiet. My grandmother founded the order on the difference.

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll walk the line."; or player says: "Then I'll go look at faces."*

> Hale, first waystation out of Dawnmead. Odessa at the long meadow. Brant at the fork. Edda at the top, the Last Lamp. Say I sent you and nothing else. They'll know.

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_offer__declined`** — *player says: "That's a long road."*

> It is. That's rather the point of it.

### Conversation: `q_the_lamps_of_the_line_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_lamps_of_the_line:ready)*

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Four posts, four reports. Hale's quiet, Odessa's counting wolves, Brant's watching the trees, and Edda's still standing the worst mile. That's the line, held.

**`q_the_lamps_of_the_line_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> My grandmother said it once and we've been repeating it ever since: the lamp stays lit. She'd have liked you. She liked almost no one. Here's your wages.

### Conversation: `q_the_last_patrol_active` *(plays when: quest:the_last_patrol:active)*

**`q_the_last_patrol_active__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> weathered letter Give it here.

**`q_the_last_patrol_active__read`** — *follows straight on from "hub"*

> 'Back before the thaw.' And the oath at the bottom, written small, the way you write a thing you mean. This is the winter patrol. Lost before my time. Not before my grandmother's.

**`q_the_last_patrol_active__ask`** — *follows straight on from "read"*

> The dead that walk where they fell don't get to keep walking. Put the watch and their shieldmen to rest, and I'll enter the letter in the rolls with the patrol marked home. That's the whole of what the order can still do for them. It's not nothing.

**`q_the_last_patrol_active__where`** — *player says: "Where did they fall?"*

> Where the old dead stand now. The ruined tower on the first climb keeps its garrison after dark, and the deeper crypts keep the rest. You'll know the watch by their shields. They kept those, at least.

**`q_the_last_patrol_active__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll see them to rest."; or follows straight on from "where"*

> The lamp stays lit. Go.

### Conversation: `q_the_last_patrol_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_last_patrol:ready)*

**`q_the_last_patrol_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Done? Done, then. The rolls.

## Mistress Petra `mason_petra` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Granite hands, chalk-line eye. Her guild raised the terraces you're standing on, and she can tell you which course her grandfather laid.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Mason who swung the pick through her own grandfather's sealwork on Maren's order. Technical, defensive-precise; over-explains joints and loads when the real subject gets close. The engineering talk is armor.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/spark_wren` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.689 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `mason_petra__bark_2` — "My grandfather helped set the Undercroft seal. Last month I swung the first pick that broke it. Family trade, both directions."
- `mason_petra__bark_3` — "Stone doesn't lie, doesn't hurry, doesn't forgive. Best colleague I ever had."

### Conversation: `petra_seal`

**`petra_seal__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Guild yard. Mind the stock, the pillars bite. Petra, master mason. Every course of every terrace you climbed today was guild work. Most of it my family's cutting.

**`petra_seal__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "seal"; or follows straight on from "below"*

> What's your question, then?

**`petra_seal__seal`** — *player says: "You broke the seal yourself?"*

> First pick, my own swing. The Warden gave the order, but the guild insisted the breaking be ours. My grandfather helped SET those stones, after the trouble took the deep crews. Twenty years the guild kept that seal pointed and tight. His initials were under my pick when I swung. I don't have a word for what that is. 'Family trade' is as close as I've got.

**`petra_seal__below`** — *player says: "What did you find below?"*

> The old works, standing. Every bench where the crews left it, the stock still racked, one brazier the guild's kept fed by way of the ledge crack all these years. Don't ask. Guild secret. The answer is stubbornness. And the market floor was swept. Twenty years sealed, and swept. Kobolds don't sweep. We put it in the report and none of us has mentioned it since, which tells you what the guild thinks of it.

**`petra_seal__guild`** — *player says: "Tell me about the guild."*

> The Masons raised the terraces in my great-great-grandmother's time. Cut the stair, hung the arches. The guild law is one line: stone outlasts the reasons. Build so the work still deserves to stand after the reasons are forgotten. The Undercroft was guild work twice over, the building and the sealing.

**`petra_seal__bye`** — *player says: "Solid work, Mistress."*

> Mind the edge on the stair.

## Queen Kayri `queen_kayri` — 14 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Pale as fresh snow on the Crown terrace, and never more than a glance from the King's side. She watches a room the way a ferryman watches water, pleasantly and missing nothing.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Ford-born queen who audited the king's own arithmetic. The sharpest wit in the game. Quick, precise, auditor's eye; affection expressed as correction. Every line lands exactly where she aimed it.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/spite_vex` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.711 · cfg 0.569

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `queen_kayri__bark_1` — "I grew up at the ford, counting toll wagons. I married up the mountain and now I count everything else."
- `queen_kayri__bark_2` — "The court gave us matching thrones and Aeriex had Stig the carpenter move them together the same week. A hand's reach, he said, or what's the point of two."
- `queen_kayri__bark_3` — "Aeriex signs the charters. I read them first. That is the whole secret of the Silver Line."

### Conversation: `kayri_mere`

**`kayri_mere__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You needn't bow. The forecourt does enough of that for everyone. You have road dust on you. Good. The interesting visitors always do.

**`kayri_mere__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Something else."; or follows straight on from "work"*

> Walk with me a moment. The court can spare me; it mostly needs me to have opinions later.

**`kayri_mere__ford`** — *player says: "You're from Amberford, aren't you?"*

> Ford-born and proud of it. My mother pulled toll wagons out of the mud during the war years; I counted them through from the bank steps. When Aeriex came down-mountain to sign the peace ledgers, he added his sums wrong twice and I corrected him twice, out loud, in front of his guards. He says that's when he decided. I say a queen who can audit a toll book is worth two who can dance.

**`kayri_mere__work`** — *player says: "What does a queen actually do here?"*

> I read everything before he signs it. Charters, tithes, the Waykeepers' muster, Odele's quarter-ledgers. A crown is mostly arithmetic wearing jewelry. At midday I walk to the mere and let the city pretend it doesn't see me. The gossip I overhear on the way is worth half of what the council tells me, and it rhymes better.

**`kayri_mere__mere`** — *player says: "Tell me about the Mirrormere."*

> Everything below us starts as this one still sheet of water: the falls, the Roaring Pool, the channel the whole city drinks from. I walk there when I need reminding that the quiet things run the loud ones. Sella would call that a sermon. I call it water finding its level.

**`kayri_mere__bye`** — *player says: "Grace to you, my Queen."*

> Grace to you, traveler. Spend your coin on Lantern Row. I'll hear about it if you don't.

**`kayri_mere__errand`** — *player says: "Peld and Perl have your word."*

> I know. I audited your delivery through channels you needn't worry about. The sums came back whole. There aren't many I'd trust with childhood debts. Consider yourself entered in the good column.

### Conversation: `q_the_queens_ford_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_queens_ford:available)*

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> My husband sends you at brigands; I have a smaller sum. I'm ford-born, Amberford, before the arithmetic found me. Two people there are owed a word I can't deliver without it becoming a procession. Will you carry it plainly?

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__who`** — *player says: "Who are they to you?"*

> Peld taught me the river's moods and never once charged me the crossing. Goodwife Perl's orchard fed me fruit that, audit the phrasing carefully, wasn't strictly mine. Childhood debts. The interest compounds.

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."; or player says: "Then I'll settle them."*

> Peld first, at the ferry: Kayri still counts the crossings. Then Perl, among the oaks: the debt is remembered. Bring back what Perl says word for word. I'll know if you round it.

**`q_the_queens_ford_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'm no messenger."*

> Mm. Neither was I, and look what they did with me.

### Conversation: `q_the_queens_ford_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_queens_ford:ready)*

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Report.

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__word`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

> Peld looked at the water, and Perl said the trees remember me taller than I was. That's her exactly. You didn't round it.

**`q_the_queens_ford_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "word"*

> The sum balances. Take the traveler's cape: ford wool, not court silk. I checked the provenance myself. You'll get more use from it than the court would.

## Scrivener Tove `scrivener_tove` — 6 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Spectacles, ink to the second knuckle, and the serene confidence of somebody whose maps have never gotten anyone lost.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Scrivener of Inks and Charts; wants the world written down before it changes. Enthusiastic pedant; measures distance in days-walked; corrects maps mid-conversation. Delight is the engine.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/sunny_posy` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.756 · cfg 0.534

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `scrivener_tove__bark_1` — "Deeds, charters, wills, and maps. I write all four and I keep a copy of all four."
- `scrivener_tove__bark_2` — "Keep your own chart as you travel. A bought map only shows where the mapmaker went."
- `scrivener_tove__bark_3` — "The Guildhall's records room and I disagree about seventeen boundary stones. I'm right about sixteen and stubborn about the last."

### Conversation: `tove_charts`

**`tove_charts__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the wet ink, that's someone's inheritance drying. Welcome to Inks & Charts. Deeds, charters, wills, and honest maps. And yes, before you ask, the maps are the interesting part. They are ALWAYS the interesting part.

**`tove_charts__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "maps"; or follows straight on from "deeds"*

> What can I draw up for you?

**`tove_charts__maps`** — *player says: "What makes a map honest?"*

> An honest map shows its ignorance. Mine have blank patches labeled I have not been here, and neither has anyone I trust. A map that guesses sends confident people into the Thornveil at dusk. Three days' walk south-southwest, roughly. Don't quote the roughly. The Guildhall buys my charts because they admit what they don't know.

**`tove_charts__deeds`** — *player says: "You keep the city's papers?"*

> Every deed on Lantern Row, half the mining claims on the Emberway, and the boundary rolls that the Guildhall's records room and I fight over, politely. Seventeen disputed stones between us. I'm right about sixteen. The seventeenth I defend on principle. I'll concede it after a survey and not before.

**`tove_charts__advice`** — *player says: "Any advice for a traveler?"*

> Keep your own chart. Mark it as you walk. A bought map only shows where the mapmaker was willing to go. Yours shows where you went. When you've filled a whole province with your own footsteps, come back and tell me what my maps got wrong. I'll pay in ink and gratitude. Mostly ink.

**`tove_charts__bye`** — *player says: "Ink and luck, Scrivener."*

> Ink and luck. Come back with corrections.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__word`** — *player says: "What's the word?"*

> That the flame is tended. And that I still set a bowl for her at midwinter. She won't say much back. That's how you'll know it landed.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."*

> Down the High Road, past the fork, up where the weather starts arguing. Her lamp is the one that doesn't go out.

**`q_the_sisters_lamp_offer__declined`** — *player says: "My boots are done for now."*

> Then warm them here a while. The word has kept for years; it keeps a little more.

### Conversation: `sella_shrine`

**`sella_shrine__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Peace at the top of the road, traveler. This is the Silver Shrine. The mother-flame of every lamp in the Dawnlands. You've walked past a dozen of its children to stand here.

**`sella_shrine__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "flame"; or follows straight on from "edda"*

> Warm yourself. Ask, if asking's why you climbed.

**`sella_shrine__flame`** — *player says: "What is the mother-flame?"*

> Older than the city. The shepherds kept it on this shore before the first terrace was cut. A fire against the dark that has never gone out. Every road lamp from here to the ford was first lit from a wick carried down this hill. That's the whole of it, truly: the dark is large, and we pass the light along.

**`sella_shrine__edda`** — *player says: "Edda of the Last Lamp is your sister?"*

> My elder sister. The family stubbornness went to her, with interest. Forty years ago she carried a wick down the mountain and planted it at the worst mile of the road. On purpose. 'The flame belongs where the dark is thickest, Sella. Not where the view is nice.' She still writes twice a year to check I haven't let the mother go out. I answer politely. Both times.

**`sella_shrine__bless`** — *player says: "May I light a thought before the road?"*

> Then light it. There. The flame doesn't grant things. That isn't its work. It remembers you asked, at every lamp you pass, in every window at dusk, all the way down the mountain. Travelers say the road feels shorter afterward. I don't argue with them.

**`sella_shrine__bye`** — *player says: "Peace on your mountain, Keeper."*

> Peace on your road. Pass the light along.

**`q_the_silver_setting_offer__what`** — *player says: "What's the commission?"*

**`q_the_silver_setting_turnin__closed`** — *follows straight on from "paid"*

### Conversation: `vigdis_setting`

**`vigdis_setting__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

**`vigdis_setting__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or player says: "Something else."; or follows straight on from "stamp"*

> Browsing, buying, or after stories?

**`vigdis_setting__work`** — *player says: "What comes off your bench?"*

> Rings, settings, seals, circlets. Small work, held to closer measures than anything else on this mountain. My furnace is the smallest flame up here. Balla up at the Grand Forge makes the mountain useful. I make it beautiful. Thirty years we've argued over which is harder.

**`vigdis_setting__stamp`** — *player says: "Why assay-stamped silver only?"*

> Runa's stamp or no sale. That's my one commandment. Runa keeps the assay counter, and her stamp says a bar has a history: this vein, this pour, this weight, witnessed. Set one ring in unstamped silver and the whole shop's word goes with it. If a stranger in an alley offers you mountain silver without a stamp, you've met the Rookery. Count your fingers after the handshake.

**`vigdis_setting__crown`** — *player says: "You've made things for the Crown?"*

> The Queen's circlet. She asked for plain, and plain is the hardest work I've done. There's nowhere for a flaw to hide. The toll-house seal at the ford came off this bench too; every stamped wagon south of here answers to a die I cut. And once, a matched pair of rings for the King, who paid full price and waited his turn behind a miner buying a wedding band. That's the Line for you.

**`vigdis_setting__browse`** — *player says: "Show me your wares."*

> The cases, then. Everything stamped, everything priced, everything exactly what it claims.

**`vigdis_setting__bye`** — *player says: "Shine on, Silversmith."*

> Shine on. And have a look at the Row's lamps on your way out.

### Conversation: `koll_pour`

**`koll_pour__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

**`koll_pour__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "pour"; or follows straight on from "balla"*

**`koll_pour__pour`** — *player says: "Walk me through the pour."*

Three furnaces, oldest to newest: the Widow, the Bride, and the third one, which we don't name, because naming them is what spoiled the first two's luck. That's not superstition. That's furnace management. Silver looks done four minutes before it is. Count the four minutes.

**`koll_pour__balla`** — *player says: "You and Balla feud, I hear."*

Her quenches run true and her steel's the best on the mountain, and if you tell her I said that I'll swear you misheard it over the bellows.

**`koll_pour__tithe`** — *player says: "What's the tithe like?"*

> Every tenth bar walks next door to Runa's scales for the Crown. I'll say this for the Line: the tithe pays for the shoring, the braziers, and the watch on the wall, and Runa's never skimmed a grain in her life. I pour eleven bars a batch so I never have to count in front of her.

**`koll_pour__bye`** — *player says: "Keep your fires, Smeltmaster."*

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

### Conversation: `ansgar_stores`

**`ansgar_stores__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Mind the pass, the soup goes through at speed. You are welcome in my kitchens, traveler, provided you stand somewhere the work is not.

**`ansgar_stores__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "feed"; or follows straight on from "crown"*

> Ask, while the bread proves.

**`ansgar_stores__feed`** — *player says: "How do you feed a castle up a mountain?"*

> Grain up the High Road from Amberford, greens off the Greenstair, fish out of two waters, salt when Saltmere's carts feel brave. Four hundred meals a week from five hearths. A castle is not a fortress, traveler. It is a list, and I keep it. The fortress part is what happens if I stop.

**`ansgar_stores__crown`** — *player says: "What are the King and Queen like to serve?"*

> The King eats what the garrison eats and notices if it is better. The Queen reads my ledger for sport and has found one error in six years. I leave her one small one a month now, seeded fair. She knows. She finds it anyway, and writes SEEN beside it in a hand like a knife.

**`ansgar_stores__signy`** — *player says: "Signy at the cookhouse says her kitchen feeds the real city."*

> She is entirely right and I will deny saying so. Signy feeds two districts on shift bells with no ceremony to hide behind. I feed one castle that would eat ceremony if I let it. When her stores run short mine walk down the stair after dark, and no ledger of mine records the walk.

**`ansgar_stores__bye`** — *player says: "I'll leave you to the proving."*

> Safe roads. Eat before the climb down, it is longer than it looks.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `warden_maren__bark_3` — "Silverfall is not a city with a mine. It is a mine that learnt manners."

### Conversation: `maren_fine` *(plays when: faction:crown:atmost:outlaw)*

**`maren_fine__greet`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "quote"*

> You stand in the crown's debt. There is a number. Pay it, or carry it.

**`maren_fine__quote`** — *player says: "What's the number?"*

> She reads the ledger once, and doesn't read it again.

**`maren_fine__pay`** — *player says: "I'll pay it."*

> She waits with her hand open.

**`maren_fine__bye`** — *player says: "I'll carry it."*

> Then carry it where the guard can see you.

### Conversation: `maren_hold`

**`maren_hold__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> You've climbed a long way to stand in a drafty hall. Welcome to it. I'm Maren. Castellan of Castle Silverfall. The charter says High Warden. The work is the same under either name.

**`maren_hold__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "kobolds"; or follows straight on from "hard"*

> Ask what you came to ask.

**`maren_hold__seal`** — *player says: "You broke the Undercroft seal. Why?"*

> The upper veins are thinning, and Solvei's surveys finally frightened me in the right direction. A city that lives by silver cannot spend a generation pretending its own cellar isn't there. The Masons counseled patience. I ordered the breaking, and Petra swung the pick through her own grandfather's stonework. If the dark sends up more than ore, the account is mine to settle. I said so at the moot.

**`maren_hold__kobolds`** — *player says: "And the kobolds?"*

> Still down there. We hold the market spine and the swept galleries. Past the rubble line, the warren holds itself. Grettir's crews go armed and come back counted. For now the account balances. Travelers who tilt it in our favor find the city grateful. In coin.

**`maren_hold__hard`** — *player says: "That was a hard call."*

> All the calls up here are hard. I weigh them as long as the day allows, then I stand by them. I won't say more than that.

**`maren_hold__city`** — *player says: "What is Silverfall, to you?"*

> A mine that learnt manners. The terraces, the banners, the court: all of it is what the silver bought. Put your ear to any wall on a quiet night and you'll hear picks.

**`maren_hold__hold`** — *player says: "What should I know about the Hold?"*

> The feast hall seats the moot. The armory arms the watch, and the wardens' wing sleeps light. The Mirrormere behind us feeds the falls, the falls feed the pool, and the pool has caught three careless wardens that the histories admit to. Mind the edge. It's the city motto for good reason.

**`maren_hold__bye`** — *player says: "Thank you, High Warden."*

> The road down is easier than the road up. Walk well.

### Conversation: `q_the_crowns_count_offer` *(plays when: quest:the_crowns_count:available)*

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> The crown counts service. Kobolds press the deep galleries below the city. Six fewer would be service. I weighed easier terms. There aren't any.

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "Six, then."*

> The galleries are reached through the Undercroft. Come back counted.

**`q_the_crowns_count_offer__declined`** — *player says: "I'll think on it."*

> Think where the crown can't hear you at it.

### Conversation: `q_the_crowns_count_turnin` *(plays when: quest:the_crowns_count:ready)*

**`q_the_crowns_count_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Six. The count moves, and the crown remembers the direction. So do I.

*Thread-ends pinned to her sleeve in an order that is absolutely a filing system. The Hold's banners were born on her looms.*

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `weaver_ottilie__bark_3` — "Lowland cotton, mountain wool, deep gloomsilk. It all comes to my loom eventually."

### Conversation: `ottilie_loom`

**`ottilie_loom__greet`** — *opens the conversation*

> Welcome to the artisans' hall. Looms left, carving right, commissions by appointment. I'm Ottilie. Mind the thread tension.

**`ottilie_loom__hub`** — *follows straight on from "greet"; or follows straight on from "banners"; or follows straight on from "cloth"*

> Yes?

**`ottilie_loom__banners`** — *player says: "You wove the Hold's banners?"*

> Every one. The Warden asked for 'something dignified' and I delivered dignity with one thread of arrogance woven through the field: silver on silver, visible only when the hall fires gutter. Twenty years and nobody's spotted it. Maren would approve, which is why I'll never tell her.

**`ottilie_loom__cloth`** — *player says: "Where does mountain cloth come from?"*

> Lowland cotton up the High Road. Mountain wool off the Greenstair rams. And lately, gloomsilk thread out of the deep. Yes, spider-spun, and no, I will not apologize for it. It takes dye like nothing under the sun and drapes like falling water.

**`ottilie_loom__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the bolts."*

> Bolts and thread, mountain grade. If it frays before the year turns, bring it back.

### Conversation: `q_threads_of_the_row_offer` *(plays when: quest:threads_of_the_row:available)*

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__hub`** — *opens the conversation*

> You sew. I can see it in how you stand near the looms. Respectfully. Very well. I have a commission I won't describe, and a shortage: eight lengths of gloomsilk thread, four bolts of linen.

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__dead`** — *player says: "Gloomsilk. That means the dead."*

> It means the crypts and the deep spiders, yes. Grave-spun, cold to the hand. There is no substitute, which is why the commission pays. Beauty is labor. Some labor is dark.

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__sworn`** — *player says: "I'll bring the lot."; or player says: "Then I'll labor."*

> The linen you may weave from honest scrap like anyone else. Bring me both, and the Row will pay you in cloth worth wearing.

**`q_threads_of_the_row_offer__declined`** — *player says: "Find someone else, Master Weaver."; or player says: "Find someone else."*

> Hm. The shortage remains. It does not care that you refused.

### Conversation: `q_threads_of_the_row_turnin` *(plays when: quest:threads_of_the_row:ready)*

**`q_threads_of_the_row_turnin__paid`** — *opens the conversation*

> Lay it out. The thread is true-spun and the linen is even. From field-taught hands, that is a small astonishment. The Row pays: two bolts of finished gloomsilk, woven here, worth more than the coin beside them. Wear it or sell it. If you sell it, sell it proudly. It came off my looms.

## Varga `broker_varga` — 4 dialogue lines, 3 quips and barks

*Scales true to the grain, and an eye truer. Every barrow of deep ore crosses her counter before it sees daylight.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Ore broker of the Deep Market; every barrow crosses her counter and every rumor gets a price. Quick, numeric, friendly the way scales are friendly. The smile is part of the transaction.

**Chatterbox casting:** `rpg_fantasy/female/flint_greta` *(provisional)* · exaggeration 0.711 · cfg 0.551

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `broker_varga__bark_1` — "Ore bought, ore sold, weighed in front of you. Nothing down here to distract a scale."
- `broker_varga__bark_2` — "Bursar Odele takes my ledger up the stair every night. We have never disagreed by so much as a pebble."
- `broker_varga__bark_3` — "Mithril? Adamant? Walk the galleries with your own pick. Starfall? Walk faster than the spider."

### Conversation: `varga_scales`

**`varga_scales__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "trade"; or follows straight on from "advice"*

> Ore bought, ore sold, everything weighed where you can watch the needle. What's your business?

**`varga_scales__trade`** — *player says: "What moves through the deep trade?"*

> Silver out of the swept faces, iron and coal steady, and the first mithril dust anyone's weighed in twenty years. The old galleries run richer than the yard's, which is why half of Grettir's shift keeps asking to come down. Everything crosses this counter, gets its chalk mark, and walks up the stair to the bank at close.

**`varga_scales__advice`** — *player says: "Any advice for a gallery run?"*

> Chalk your name at the landing. Keep to the swept walks your first three trips. I count trips, it's what I do. And price the starfall honestly: the vein is real, the spider is realer, and the digmaster's tunnel gets closer to both every week. Come back with ore, I pay fair. Come back empty and alive, I call it a profit anyway. Broker's discretion.

**`varga_scales__browse`** — *player says: "Show me the scales."*

> The counter's yours. Weighed to the grain, priced to the day.

*Ash-grey, quick-fingered, and wearing nine brass rings that are absolutely not all his. The deep's oddities find his stall the way water finds low ground.*

**Who they are, and how to say it:** Curio barker, the one licensed showman below ground. Patter, invented provenance, self-mythology he may not believe either. Exclamatory, list-happy, every line a small performance for a crowd of one.

### Ambient barks — said in passing; the game matches your recording to the shown line, so record VERBATIM

- `curio_ninebrass__bark_1` — "Curios, oddments, and things the dark coughed up. Every piece with a story, half the stories true."
- `curio_ninebrass__bark_2` — "The glowshroom grotto grows my lamp-mushrooms, the cistern grows blindfish, and the galleries grow rumors. I sell all three."
- `curio_ninebrass__bark_3` — "Was I here before the seal broke? Now that's a premium story, friend. It costs more than you're holding."

### Conversation: `ninebrass_stall`

**`ninebrass_stall__hub`** — *opens the conversation; or follows straight on from "stock"; or follows straight on from "before"*

> Curios! Oddments! Things the dark coughed up and I dusted off! Every piece has a story, half the stories are true, and the true ones cost extra! What catches your eye?

**`ninebrass_stall__stock`** — *player says: "Where does your stock come from?"*

> The grotto grows my lamp-shrooms! The cistern gives up blindfish bones carved prettier than they've any right to be! And the galleries produce what galleries produce: ember-stones, frost-shards, dust that remembers being Arx. The miners bring it up, I dust it off, you carry it away. The deep provides, friend. The deep PROVIDES.

**`ninebrass_stall__before`** — *player says: "Were you down here before the seal broke?"*

> Ahhh, THE question. Everyone asks. The price keeps going up. I'll say this much for free: the seal was built to keep things out. Nobody ever asked it to keep things in. The floor didn't sweep itself, the brazier in the old works didn't feed itself, and Ninebrass didn't teach himself to haggle in the dark. Or I walked down with the guild crews like everyone else and I'm salting my legend. That's the beauty of the deep, friend. Both stories weigh the same.

**`ninebrass_stall__browse`** — *player says: "Let me see the strange stuff."*

> Browse, browse! Mind the frost-shard, it holds grudges.
